Valuation Methodology and Risks

                        Unimicron (3037.TW)

                        Base case, residual income (RI) valuation model, which we think derives the most accurate
                        value of the firm given that it takes into account cost of equity. We use a cost of equity of 9.2%
                        [risk-free rate of 1% (10-year Taiwan government note yield), equity risk premium of 8.7%, and
                        a beta of 1.0], a medium-term growth rate of 14%, and a terminal growth rate of 3%.

                        Risks to Upside

                           n Better-than-expected ABF substrate demand from PC and server customers
                           n Capex cuts; halt to its capacity expansion plan
                           n Continued yield issues of alternative technology that doesn't require substrate (e.g.,
                              CoWoP)

                        Risks to Downside

                           n Sudden demand shortfall
                           n Technological change that would not require ABF substrates
                           n Intensifying competition
                           n Yield issues or production hiccups when ramping new capacity

Valuation Methodology and Risks

                        Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (6770.TW)

                        Base case, 2.0x 2027e P/B. This method is in line with our approach for Greater China memory
                        IDM players, in view of the industry's high volatility. Our 2.0x target P/B is higher than the
                        historical average of 1.5x since 2021, reflecting our optimistic view on improved pricing and
                        utilization.

                        Risks to Upside

                           n Pricing power is sustained in 2026.
                           n Listing on main board attracts investment fund flows.
                           n Aluminum process enjoys higher margins.

                        Risks to Downside

                           n Competition from China intensifies.
                           n Price erosion is faster than expected.
                           n Demand from consumer electronics clients weakens further.
                           n Inventory in the supply chain takes longer to digest.

                                             Mediatek
                                             Company description
                                             Mediatek (MTK) is a fabless IC company that designs SoC for smartphone,
                                             smart TV, and digital media devices. It also develops chips for connectivity,
                                             networking, smart home gadgets, and automotive sectors. It was founded in
                                             1997, is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange, and is headquartered in Taiwan.
                                             It has sales and research subsidiaries in mainland China, Singapore, India,
                                             the US, Japan, Korea, Denmark, and England. It primarily sells its products in
                                             China and other emerging-market countries.

                                             Investment strategy
                                             We rate Mediatek shares as Buy. We expect Mediatek to ride on 5G migration
                                             in emerging markets and market share gain of its high-end Dimensity series in
                                             China market as well. In particular, we see strong growth potential from its AI
                                             ASIC, NTN-satellite business in the long term. We believe solid fundamentals
                                             and strong operating leverage will support Mediatek’s margins outlook.

                                             Valuation
                                             Our NT$6,800 target price (rounded) for Mediatek is based on 30x P/E to
                                             2027/2028 EPS, which is 1-std above its five-year average forward P/E given
                                             the promising outlook from its AI ASIC business starting from 2H26. We
                                             believe our target PE is also justified by Mediatek's global and regional peers'
                                             trading at an average of c32x PER. AI ASIC development with CSPs should
                                             provide more upside from 2027 onwards. We also see Mediatek as well
                                             prepared for 6G and 6G+NTN Satellite communication. Despite lukewarm
                                             smartphone overall deamand, we expect Mediatek to benefit from 5G
                                             migration in emerging markets and its Dimensity series should also gain
                                             shares in flagship models. Non-smartphone business is also seeing
                                             stabilizing TV and IoT demand with Mediatek outgrowing the overall market
                                             on its better technology in WiFi 7 and connectivity.

                                             Risks
                                             Key downside risks that could prevent the shares from reaching our target
                                             price include: 1) weaker-than-expected growth from AI ASIC business; 2)
                                             more severe competition in the smartphone segment; 3) slower overall
                                             demand related to macroeconomic risks, especially for smartphone demand;
                                             and 4) further price hikes from foundries.

MULTI-INDUSTRY

         Primer on 800VDC and implications for Electricals companies


Investor debate this year has been increasingly focused on NVIDIA's 800VDC architecture and the race among
Electrical OEMs to develop the necessary product portfolios. These technological shifts are likely to reshape the
competitive landscape. In this report, we outline the importance of these technologies, map the current competitive
environment for 800VDC electrical equipment, and review the positioning, development efforts, and recent
progress of companies across our Electricals coverage. Within our European coverage, we see the best valuation
opportunity on the data center demand topic in Legrand (upgraded to Buy today) and to a lesser extent Siemens
(Buy).

The transition to 800VDC power distribution is primarily driven by the need to resolve the physical and
electrical bottlenecks associated with scaling next-generation AI workloads, where rack power densities are
surging from tens of kilowatts to over 1MW per rack. This architecture will enable higher power efficiency, up to 45%
reduction in copper mass, and better management of volatile load swings. Key products being developed include
upstream MV UPS and rack-adjacent sidecars for hybrid set-ups, SSTs or MV rectifiers for primary conversion, high-
efficiency DC-DC converters, solid-state breakers, and advanced energy storage systems (CESS/BESS). We assess
volume impacts by product from 800VDC in Exhibit 4.

The competitive landscape for 800VDC products spans electrical incumbents, solar inverter manufacturers,
and pure-play SST start-ups. We highlight that there are differences in terms of the chosen product pathways as
well as expected timelines for hybrid AC/DC retrofits and fully native 800VDC architectures. Among incumbents,
Legrand, Schneider, Eaton, Vertiv and Delta appear to have the most complete offerings, both for traditional
products (spanning the power train, cooling infrastructure and networking infrastructure, Exhibit 4) as well as
800VDC-adapted products (with all of them planning to offer sidecars and being in the process of
developing/commercializing SSTs). In particular, we note that Legrand's product portfolio announcements at its
CMD exceeded our expectations, highlighted by the introduction of a new sidecar, organic liquid cooling
solutions, and AI-load stabilizers, as well as indications of the development of an SST (see here). These
additions establish a nearly complete product suite, diversifying away from the company's traditional concentration
in white space infrastructure; one of the key thesis points for our upgrade to Buy.

Other key areas of technology that have come into focus with the transition to 800VDC include specialized
cabling and liquid cooling. Lower current requirements allow thinner, smaller cables, and, while lower copper
tonnage may represent a volume headwind, this transition could be margin-accretive for leading European cable
manufacturers Prysmian (Buy) and Nexans (Buy) due to higher engineered ASPs. The concentration of power in
next-gen AIDCs is also likely to accelerate the adoption of High-Temperature Superconducting (HTS) cables,
where Nexans is a market pioneer. Liquid cooling has also emerged as a key necessity for sustaining MW-scale rack
loads in 800VDC data centers, whether hybrid or complete. Envicool and Vertiv have broad offerings comprising cold
plates, piping and CDUs, while Alfa Laval is the market leader in copper-brazed heat exchangers used in CDUs.
 PM Summary
Investor debate has been increasingly focused on NVIDIA's 800VDC architecture and the race among Electrical
OEMs to develop the necessary product portfolios, notably Solid-State Transformers (SSTs). These
technological shifts are likely to reshape the competitive landscape. In this report, we outline the importance of
these technologies, map the current competitive landscape for 800VDC electrical equipment, and review the
positioning, development efforts, and recent progress of companies across our Electricals coverage. Within our
European coverage, we see the best valuation opportunity on the data center demand topic in Legrand (upgraded to
Buy today) and to a lesser extent Siemens (Buy) - Exhibit 2.

The transition to 800VDC power distribution is primarily driven by the need to resolve the physical and
electrical bottlenecks associated with scaling next-generation AI workloads, where rack power densities are
surging from tens of kilowatts to over 1MW per rack. This architecture will enable higher power efficiency, up to 45%
reduction in copper mass, and better management of volatile load swings. Key products being developed include
upstream MV UPS and rack-adjacent sidecars for hybrid set-ups, SSTs or MV rectifiers for primary conversion, high-
efficiency DC-DC converters, solid-state breakers, and advanced energy storage systems (CESS/BESS). We assess
volume impacts by product from 800VDC in Exhibit 4.

The competitive landscape for 800VDC products spans electrical incumbents, solar inverter manufacturers,
and pure-play SST start-ups. We highlight that there are differences in terms of the chosen product pathways
as well as expected timelines for hybrid AC/DC retrofits and fully native 800VDC architectures. Among
incumbents, we highlight Legrand, Schneider, Eaton, Vertiv and Delta as appearing to have the most complete
offerings, both for traditional products (spanning the power train, cooling infrastructure and networking
infrastructure, Exhibit 4) as well as 800VDC-adapted products (with all of them planning to offer sidecars and being
in the process of developing/commercializing SSTs). In particular, we note that Legrand's product portfolio
announcements at its CMD exceeded our expectations, highlighted by the introduction of a new sidecar, organic
liquid cooling solutions, and AI-load stabilizers, as well as indications of the development of an SST (see our note
here). These additions establish a nearly complete product suite, diversifying the company beyond its traditional
concentration in white space infrastructure, one of the key thesis points for our upgrade to Buy.

As for SSTs, Delta Electronics, Eaton, ABB, and Schneider Electric appear to be the most advanced in SST
development, having comprehensively outlined their planned SST product portfolios with a view to shipping
them by 2H27. Other players include European incumbents Siemens (which has partnered with Reinhausen to
develop modular MV SSTs) and Legrand (which is developing an SST but remains uncertain about the ROI of
commercialization). In North America, GE Vernova has been developing both MV UPS and SST, but the company sees
the latter as still 12-24 months away from deployment. Solar inverter companies Enphase Energy and SolarEdge are
leveraging their software-defined power electronics expertise to develop GaN- or SiC-based SST solutions, although
important questions remain regarding their ability to meet the stringent requirements of mission-critical data center
operations. We note that APAC-based companies, including Megmeet and Kstar, appear more cautious about SST
deployment, with management teams recently commenting that they do not expect volume SST adoption within the
next 1-2 years. The SST market has also seen the entry of start-ups including Heron Power, Amperesand,
Hyperscale Power, and WattEV, on which we provide further detail in the report.

Leveraging our GS Sustain team's forecasts, our GS Clean Energy team sees c.10GW of new data center
capacity using 800V GPUs in 2030 (c.6% of installed base and c.60% of new additions in 2030), resulting in a
total addressable market of up to $5bn for SSTs. We note that these estimates include both Blackwell servers
(which our Clean Energy team suggests are compatible with 800VDC architectures) and Rubin servers. If only Rubin
servers were included, this would imply c.7GW of new data center capacity using 800V GPUs in 2030 (c.4% of
installed base and c.40% of new additions in 2030). This compares with: (1) ABB's 800VDC webcast expectations
that 25%-40% of new data center additions would be based on Direct Current; (2) Legrand's recent CMD
expectations that c.40% of its expected 30GW of total DC capacity addition in 2030 would be full or hybrid LVDC;
(3) SolarEdge's analyst day forecast of a 10.3GW TAM for 800VDC in 2030; and (4) our 800VDC expert call
 highlighting expectations of 21%/17% of additions in the US/Europe in 2030. We also see scope for an up to $8bn
TAM for solid state circuit breakers, based on an estimated price of $600k/MW (5x current circuit breakers,
per our 800VDC expert call).

Other key areas of technology that have come into focus with the transition to 800VDC include specialized
cabling and liquid cooling.

   Lower current requirements allow thinner and smaller cables, implying a shift from four-wire AC to three-wire DC
   (POS/RTN/PE) distribution. While lower copper tonnage may represent a volume headwind, this transition could
   be margin-accretive for leading European cable manufacturers Prysmian (Buy) and Nexans (Buy) due to higher
   engineered ASPs. The concentration of power in next-gen AIDCs is likely to accelerate the adoption of High-
   Temperature Superconducting (HTS) cables. As highlighted by OCP and Nexans, combining 800VDC with HTS
   distribution virtually eliminates heat losses while only a fraction of the space required by conventional conductors
   is occupied. We view this as a long-term tailwind for cables; Nexans in particular is positioned as a market
   pioneer, having demonstrated LV DC HTS cables for data hall infrastructure at its Stella Nova Center and having
   unveiled its AmpaCity 700V DC microgrid pilot, which paves the way for 800VDC architectures.
   Liquid cooling has also emerged as a key necessity for sustaining MW-scale rack loads in 800VDC data centers,
   whether hybrid or complete. According to Schneider Electric, it is up to 3,000 times more effective and more
   efficient at removing heat than air. Our China Tech research team has published global server cooling TAM
   estimates that reach c.$18bn in 2027, of which nearly 90% is liquid cooling. Envicool and Vertiv have broad
   offerings comprising cold plates, piping and CDUs, while Alfa Laval is the market leader in copper-brazed heat
   exchangers used in CDUs (directly supplying eight of the top 10 CDU OEMs). Carel Industries supplies high-
   performance controllers and sensors used in liquid cooling architectures for the control of both floor-mounted
   and rack-mounted CDUs. Schneider Electric and Eaton have both gained exposure to liquid cooling through
   acquisitions.

    Top 10 Learnings

     1. 800VDC enables AI racks to scale beyond 1MW, overcoming the limits of traditional low-voltage power
        architectures. It improves power efficiency by up to 5% while reducing copper volumes by 45% and
        freeing space for compute.
     2. 800VDC reshapes the entire power train. Key products include MV UPS, sidecars, Solid State
        Transformers (SSTs), DC-DC converters, solid-state circuit breakers and advanced energy storage systems.
     3. Commercialization starts in 2027, with sidecars first in early 2027 and native 800VDC
        architectures/SSTs following in late 2027/early 2028.
     4. MW-scale racks make liquid cooling essential, while specialized cabling creates new opportunities
        despite lower copper requirements.
     5. Five incumbents stand out on breadth, with Legrand, Schneider, Eaton, Vertiv and Delta building broad
        800VDC offerings.
     6. Three players lead the SST race, with Delta, Eaton and ABB targeting shipments by 2H27.
     7. Several new challengers are entering the SST landscape, spanning solar players Enphase/SolarEdge and
        specialist start-ups. We profile six of them in this note.
     8. 800VDC could reach ~10GW of new capacity in 2030 (~6% of installed DC base), supporting a ~$5bn
        SST TAM and an up to ~$8bn solid-state breaker TAM alone.
     9. Almost all suppliers expect higher revenue per MW under 800VDC, supporting the opportunity across
        electrical equipment and cables.
   10. Within our European Capital Goods coverage, we see the best valuation opportunity on the data
        center demand topic in Legrand (which trades at materially lower multiples than peers on unwarranted
        investor views that its portfolio will remain skewed to white space categories). We also think Nexans is
        underappreciated for the potential of superconducting cables to start penetrating the DC installed base.

What is 800VDC and why is it needed?
800 Volts Direct Current (800VDC) is a higher-voltage direct current power distribution architecture proposed
by NVIDIA to replace traditional alternating current (AC) and low-voltage direct current (such as 12VDC or
54VDC) systems, in order to address the physical and electrical bottlenecks associated with scaling next-
generation AI workloads. Instead of routing power through multiple inefficient AC/DC and DC/AC conversion
stages, an 800VDC architecture centrally converts utility-supplied AC power to 800VDC at the facility level and
distributes it directly to the compute racks.
 The driver of this transition is the need to efficiently support the unprecedented power density required by
modern AI racks, which are scaling from tens of kilowatts per rack to well over a megawatt per rack (Exhibit 7),
exceeding the capabilities of traditional 54VDC or 480/415 VAC systems. NVIDIA projects that its 800VDC
architecture can reduce TCO by up to 30%, driven by improvements in efficiency, reliability, and system architecture,
as well as lower equipment maintenance costs. This can be broken down into three main factors:

1. Enabling higher power efficiency. Power consumption per server continues to increase, with the current NVDA
   DGX NVL8 architecture now requiring 3.7x the maximum power of the A100 (Exhibit 6), driving up the power
   density requirement and overall power needs. Legacy data centers require multiple AC/DC and DC/AC conversion
   stages throughout the data center powertrain. Each conversion introduces efficiency losses (typically 1%-3% per
   stage), generates additional heat, and requires equipment that consumes valuable space. As power requirements
   are likely to step up in the coming years, this power conversion loss will become more significant and much more
   costly. By replacing AC with DC power distribution, multiple conversion steps are eliminated, improving end-to-
   end efficiency by up to 5% compared with current 54V systems (see here).
2. Reduction in copper content. The amount of copper required to deliver 1MW of power to a server rack at 48V
   could be more than 500-1000lbs. Stepping up distribution voltage to 800VDC significantly reduces the current
   required for the same power (as P=VI). With lower current, a higher level of resistance can be tolerated and since
   resistance is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area of wire, cables and busbars can be made thinner
   and smaller. This enables up to 45% reduction in the copper mass required and frees up valuable physical space
   for compute hardware.
3. Managing volatile load swings. AI training and inference workloads cause rapid and substantial spikes in power
   demand. An 800VDC architecture allows for the direct integration of localized energy storage to buffer these
   swings, protecting the utility grid from instability.

What new products are required and how will current products be impacted?
The 800VDC architecture fundamentally changes how power is delivered in AI data centers (Exhibit 3), causing
a shift away from traditional LV switchgears, AC PDU and AC UPS systems towards highly specialized and streamlined
DC hardware that are designed to handle extreme power densities while maintaining rapid response times. Critical
components are likely to include:

   Power sidecars. These allow current traditional AC data centers to use high-voltage DC (HVDC) without requiring
   complex changes to rack architecture. They will be deployed as transitional modules in the first 800VDC rollout
   phase (2025-2027) ahead of fully native DC halls. They attach directly to MW-class racks, converting incoming AC
   to 800VDC and providing integrated short-duration energy storage to stabilize GPU load spikes. This design
   eliminates the need for traditional AC PDUs and UPS systems while enabling rack power to scale up to 1.2 MW.
   The following companies currently offer or are developing sidecars: Delta Electronics (debuted in early
   2026), Eaton (mentioned at DC world; already being offered for refurbishment, although no sales have been
   made yet), Flex (introduced in March 2026), Legrand (introduced at its 2026 CMD, ready for
   commercialization in 2027; the company believes it could be a permanent solution), Schneider Electric
   (already being offered; explicitly targeting racks up to 1.2MW), and Vertiv (undergoing customer validation;
   expected to launch early 2027). ABB is not developing a sidecar, as the company views it as a temporary solution
   for hybrid architectures that would not be used in full 800VDC. Many companies think sidecars could be a
   permanent solution, either because not all DCs may become full 800VDC (hybrid might be sufficient for certain
   data centers) or because sidecars could be useful in full architecture (e.g. to stabilize loads).
   MV UPS: Operating upstream at the grid connection level (up to 34.5 kVAC), these centralized systems replace
   highly fragmented, low-voltage AC UPS systems in the white space, rendering traditional AC PDUs and AC UPS
   systems largely unnecessary. By bypassing individual, rack-specific UPS units, this set-up reduces AC PDU cabinet
   requirements by up to 75% and enables MW-scale rack densities. While legacy suppliers such as Schneider
   Electric and Legrand remain highly exposed to traditional AC PDUs and AC UPS markets, ABB currently holds
   dominant market share in MV DC UPS systems with its HiPerGuard product and believes that MV UPSs will
   not only facilitate the transition to hybrid architectures, but also be necessary for full 800VDC, as they
   provide increased energy efficiency. ABB notes that more players have entered the MV UPS space in recent
 months, which will encourage adoption by hyperscalers who often require double/multi-sourcing. These include
GE Vernova (plans to start shipping its MV UPS in mid 2027) and Vertiv (MV UPS currently in validation).
Solid-State Transformers (SSTs). These high-capacity conversion systems directly step down and convert MV
utility AC (up to 35kVAC) to a stable 800VDC output. They rely on advanced power electronics and semiconductor
switches instead of heavy copper coils and iron cores to convert and control electricity. By replacing traditional
multi-stage AC/DC transformers and centralizing the rectification process at the facility level, SSTs eliminate
redundant conversion steps, reduce physical footprint, and provide galvanic isolation with millisecond-level
response times to handle volatile AI workloads. While NVIDIA views SSTs as essential to the final, most efficient
form of 800VDC data centers, they are not currently in mass production. The roadmap for the transition to 800V
DC points to initial deployments starting as early as 2028, which has set off a race to commercialize SSTs. Various
OEMs and start-ups are in the process of developing SST solutions. Our Clean Energy team's estimates indicate
that the market for SSTs could reach as high as $5 billion in 2030 (see more details below). The key
companies that have outlined SST development plans with clear timelines include: ABB (Infinitus MV SST for
commercialization by 2H27), Schneider Electric (800VDC Power Center expected in 2H27), Eaton (MV SST
orders in 2H26 with shipments in 2H27), GE Vernova (5MW SST commercialization in 12-24 months) and
Delta Electronics (MV SSTs testing shipment late 2026-2H27). We dive deeper into SSTs, the market size, and
the relevant players later in this note.
Rectifiers: For facilities not deploying SSTs, centralized industrial-grade rectifiers can be used at the perimeter of
the data hall to perform the primary, high-ratio AC-to-DC conversion. Centralizing this conversion upstream
creates a common 800VDC distribution backbone, eliminating redundant conversion equipment, reducing heat
output in the white space, and enabling a much simpler path for integrating DC-side battery energy storage.
Among the European OEMs, Schneider Electric has highlighted its development of TRUs in conjunction with
SSTs in its 800VDC Power Center product, while Legrand has indicated a preference for developing TRUs over
SSTs, arguing that the ROI for SSTs may not justify commercialization. In North America, Flex recently
acquired EPC Power to develop both centralized rectifiers and SSTs for 800VDC, while Vertiv is developing
centralized rectifiers to complement its 800VDC sidecar.
DC-DC converters. Placed in the sidecar or directly adjacent to the GPUs on the server tray, these high-efficiency
converters utilize advanced Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductor technology to perform
a late-stage conversion to step the 800VDC bus down to 12VDC or 12.5VDC. This minimizes resistive losses near
the processor and occupies less board space than traditional multi-stage intermediate bus converters. ABB has
noted that these DC-DC converters will see strong demand under the new 800VDC architecture. Flex, Vertiv,
Eaton and Legrand have all explicitly mentioned the development of DC-DC converters for the 800VDC
transition.
Solid state breakers and switches. High voltage DC distribution introduces severe risks of electrical arcing and
fault currents due to the capacitive nature of the network. Instead of distributing AC power through numerous AC
switchboards, which are large assemblies of circuit breakers, switches, and control equipment, the 800VDC
architecture streamlines this. In 800VDC architectures, these are being replaced by ultra-fast semiconductor
circuit breakers and solid-state switches capable of detecting and isolating electrical faults within microseconds
(1000x faster than traditional circuit breakers) without mechanical wear. Various OEMs have been developing
solutions, including ABB, with its SACE Infinitus solid-state circuit breaker, and Siemens, with its Sentron
semiconductor circuit breaker and SIRIUS solid-state switching device. According to an expert call we hosted
recently (see here), solid state breakers are still very expensive at c.$600k per MW (5x the price of current circuit
breakers).
Capacitive and Battery Energy Storage Systems (CESS/BESS). The shift to 800VDC data centers demands
greater battery storage to handle higher power volatility, with racks able to surge from 30% to 100% utilization in
milliseconds. To handle this extreme power volatility and bypass grid interconnection limits, energy storage is
expected to evolve into an active 'low-pass filter' that absorbs high-frequency spikes and smooths load ramps.
This supports a layered strategy: fast-response capacitors handle millisecond fluctuations closer to the rack, while
large BESS provide longer ride-through closer to the utility interconnection. Flex, Vertiv, nVent, Eaton, GE Vernova,
Delta Electronics and Hitachi have all included CESS/BESS in their portfolios or are developing them. In particular
for 800VDC, Flex has gained exposure to BESS technologies through its acquisition of EPC Power, and it has also
introduced a new 30kW CESS for AI workloads at COMPUTEX 2026. Vertiv's 800VDC roadmap includes outdoor-
 rated MV BESS/UPS systems while Hitachi has integrated BESS into its 800VDC power and control architecture for
the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX reference design.
Specialized DC busways and cables. With lower current requirements, cables and busbars can be made thinner
and smaller. This implies a shift from four-wire AC to three-wire DC (Positive/Return/Protective Earth,
POS/RTN/PE) systems, reducing conductor and connector complexity. While optimized, both cables and busways
remain integral components of the 800VDC power distribution. While lower copper tonnage may represent a
volume headwind, this transition could be margin-accretive for leading European cable manufacturers Prysmian
(Buy) and Nexans (Buy) due to higher engineered ASPs. This reflects the need for specialized, high-margin
cabling engineered with advanced materials to mitigate DC-specific electrical degradation (such as space charge
accumulation) and to support innovative thermal management, including integrated liquid-cooling technologies.
Furthermore, the concentration of power in next-gen AIDCs is likely to accelerate the adoption of High-
Temperature Superconducting (HTS) cables. HTS operate at -200°C, a temperature that can be reached using
liquid nitrogen (an abundant, inexpensive and environmentally harmless coolant) and, unlike conventional copper
or aluminium cables, which lose 5%-10% of transmitted power as heat over long distances (see here), HTS cables
conduct electricity with virtually zero resistance. As highlighted by OCP, superconductors are particularly
important for AIDCs, in parallel with 800VDC, given they provide high current density with negligible energy
losses while occupying only a fraction of the space required by conventional conductors. The total
addressable market for superconducting cables (including for data centers) has been estimated at c.$1.8bn in
2025 with the potential to grow to c.$3.6bn by 2034, as per third party sources (Fortune Business Insights, S&S
Insider, Transparency Market Research). We have also seen third party estimates mentioning Nexans' market share
at 10-24% depending on the application. We view this as a long-term tailwind for the cables sector. Nexans is a
market pioneer, having demonstrated LV DC HTS cables for data hall infrastructure at its Stella Nova Center and
having recently unveiled its AmpaCity 700V DC microgrid pilot, which paves the way for 800VDC architectures. At
our recent US roadshow with Nexans, the company flagged that superconductivity could offer a compelling total
cost of ownership and recurring project revenues. However, primary drawbacks of superconductivity include
higher upfront capital expenditure and operational complexities surrounding active liquid nitrogen refrigeration
(required to enable HTS operating temperatures).


 800VDC and liquid cooling
 With the transition to high-density AI workloads, the extreme concentration of thermal energy within a
 highly compact physical footprint renders traditional air cooling insufficient. Liquid cooling has emerged as a
 key necessity for the transition to 800VDC, both in hybrid and full architectures. According to Schneider
 Electric, it is up to 3,000 times more effective and more efficient at removing heat than air because it
 captures heat directly at the chip level. Furthermore, the CapEx difference when liquid cooling is deployed at
 20kW/rack and 40kW/rack for the same capacity data center results in 10-14% CapEx savings. Our China
 Tech research team has published global server cooling TAM estimates that reach c.$18bn in 2027, of which
 nearly 90% is liquid cooling.

 The main components required for liquid cooling include coolant distribution units (CDUs, which circulate
 and regulate liquid coolant), cold plates (copper or aluminium plates that are mounted onto high-heat
 components to transfer heat away), coolants (formulated thermal fluids through which heat is transferred),
 and chillers (reject captured heat to outdoor atmosphere).

 Various companies offer components for liquid cooling. At Data Center World, Alfa Laval, Envicool, Vertiv
 and Schneider Electric all highlighted that liquid cooling will be crucial to sustaining MW-scale rack loads in
 800VDC data centers. Envicool and Vertiv have broad offerings comprising cold plates, piping and CDUs,
 while Alfa Laval is the market leader in copper-brazed heat exchangers used in CDUs (directly supplying
 eight of the top 10 CDU OEMs). Schneider and Eaton have both gained exposure to liquid cooling through
 acquisitions, namely Motivair and Boyd, respectively, both of which are now well integrated. In particular,
 Schneider Electric offers prefabricated, high-density liquid-cooled AI clusters, which combine chillers, CDUs
 and MV switchgear.
     Carel Industries has a portfolio of components to support all major data center cooling architectures,
    including liquid cooling where it supplies high-performance controllers and sensors for the control of both
    floor-mounted and rack-mounted CDUs.

about the limitations of conventional AC architectures and recently published a joint study with BCG outlining the
efficiency, scalability and infrastructure advantages of high-voltage DC distribution (see here).

ABB has been working on HVDC and SST technologies for >10 years and, in March 2025, acquired a minority
stake in DG Matrix, a pureplay SST start-up. This gave the company exposure to the DG Matrix's Power Router
platform, which integrates multiple electrical devices into a smaller and more efficient single power management
system. DG Matrix also recently announced a commercial agreement with TerraFlow to deploy the first integrated
SST and vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB) in the US to directly power a live high-performance computing cluster.

ABB has also recently introduced its new Infinitus source-to-rack DC portfolio (described in detail during a
webinar on September 24; see here). The portfolio consists of five building blocks: 1) the powertrain that
delivers stable power from the grid (HiPerGuard MV UPS, BESS, MV switchgear); 2) AC to DC conversion outside the
white space (Infinitus SST, DC UPS and TRU), 3) DC power distribution (MNS DC switchgear, SACE DC circuit breaker,
DC switchboard), 4) DC power protection (SACE circuit breakers, Infinitus Solid State Circuit Breaker) and 5)
cooling optimization (DC variable speed drives and motors as well as batteries for CDUs). Unlike some competitors,
ABB is not involved in developing rack-level sidecar solutions, which management views as a transitional technology.

providing revenue generation from 2028 onwards. Its modular HiperGuard MV UPS connects directly to 34.5kV

necessary for full 800VDC solutions. ABB has also developed the first IEC-certified solid state breaker. Orders for
these circuit breakers have already been received from other industries, and ABB is currently in discussions with
hyperscalers and a few colocators regarding their application in data centers. Two new frames will be introduced by

Residential HVAC segment. Accordingly, we expect Carel’s HVAC and Refrigeration segments to grow at a +13.8%
and +13.2% OSG CAGR through 2030. The recent acquisition of Cotes should provide a further boost, underpinning
our forecast for a +17% adj. EPS CAGR over 2025-30E.

 Legrand (LEGD.PA; Buy, covered by Daniela Costa)

Legrand generates c.32% of group sales from data centers and the company has a broad product portfolio
including components for the powertrain and networking infrastructure (Exhibit 4). Legrand's current data
center offering can be split into: compute infrastructure (50%, includes racks, PDUs, busways and cables), critical
power (35%, includes MV switchgear, transformers, switches), advanced cooling (5%, includes rear door heat
exchangers and direct-to-chip products) and testing & lifecycle services (10%) (Exhibit 20). While Legrand is skewed
towards the white space (c.75% of its data center sales), it has been active in increasing exposure to the gray space
(which grew from 5% to 25% of data center sales between 2022 and 2025) with acquisitions such as Kratos and
Accelsius (Exhibit 21).

The transition toward 800VDC architectures has emerged as one of the key investor debates around Legrand's
long-term positioning. Given its historical strength in low voltage and white space data center products, investors
have increasingly asked questions about its ability to continue to grow its data center business in line with data
center capex. However, at its recent 2026 CMD, Legrand demonstrated its extensive product pipeline for the
transition (Exhibit 22), and now expects data center content per MW to increase from $2.5mn currently to
>$3mn for hybrid/LVDC architecture. Management expects critical power to increase the most in LVDC
architectures, compute infrastructure to increase the most in hybrid architecture, services to increase the most for
LVDC, and advanced cooling to increase for both hybrid/LVDC. Legrand is working on SSTs and estimates that $
per MW could increase to $3.8mn if SSTs were to be included. However, management has not yet made the
decision on launching this product given profitability and ROI is not certain.

At its 2026 CMD, Legrand presented its LVDC target architecture in three phases: 1) AC architecture with OCP
ORv3; 2) Sidecar architecture and 3) LVDC architecture. Phase 1 (current state of the most advanced DC
architectures) centralizes AC-DC converters in the power shelf of OCP racks and uses rear DC busbar to power them,
thus improving conversion efficiency and spatial density. Phase 2 (near term) involves taking those power shelves out
of the rack and bundling them next to the rack in a sidecar, liberating premium rack space for compute while
allowing operators to retain existing upstream AC infrastructure. Legrand has introduced its power sidecar (can
support up to 600kW with 415-480V AC input and 810V DC output), which will be ready for commercialization
in 2027 and which Legrand believes could be a permanent solution. Phase 3 (longer term) achieves end-to-end
efficiency by eliminating intermediate conversion steps, distributing LVDC directly from grid tied transformers (SSTs
or Rectifier Units) via DC busways to the IT rack. Legrand has also introduced its AI-load stabilizer; this will be
ready in 2028 and Legrand believes it will have an advantage over MV UPS, which it views as being too far from
the AI load to provide necessary protection. Legrand also highlighted its capabilities in cooling solutions, including
rear door heat exchangers and liquid-cooled load banks (which it was the first to introduce and which it highlights as
essential for any liquid cooling technology).

Infineon (IFXGn.DE; Buy, covered by Alexander Duval) is a leading semiconductor manufacturer, so, while it

partnership with DG Matrix to integrate Infineon's SiC MOSFETs into the multi-port SST platform for AI data centers
and industrial microgrids. Furthermore, in July 2026, Infineon signed an MoU to collaborate on high-efficiency direct
current power infrastructure solutions. Infineon estimates the semiconductor market for SSTs could reach up to
$1bn within the next five years, driven by rising electricity demand from AI and electrification trends.

Deep-dive into SSTs
What do transformers do and why are they important? Traditional transformers are passive electromagnetic
devices that step alternating current (AC) voltage levels up or down to enable efficient long-distance transmission
 and safe local distribution. By stepping up voltage for transmission, transformers allow the same amount of power to
be delivered at a significantly lower level of current, which minimizes resistive heat loss, reduces the required
conductor size, and lowers overall infrastructure costs. Conversely, step-down transformers are vital for the safe
distribution of electricity, reducing high transmission voltages to levels suitable for industrial and residential end-
uses. While highly reliable, their reliance on heavy iron cores and copper coils makes them bulky, heavy, and
incapable of active power management.

How are solid-state transformers (SSTs) different? SSTs, often referred to as 'smart' transformers, replace the
heavy iron cores and copper coils of traditional transformers with high-frequency power electronics by leveraging
advanced Silicon Carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) semiconductors. This allows SSTs to act as intelligent
energy routers, offering bidirectional power flow, active power management and real-time voltage regulation (in
contrast to passive traditional transformers), while also being more efficient and 50% smaller. Crucially, they are able
to convert high voltage AC to 800VDC (Exhibit 32). This typically occurs through main three stages: 1) Input stage:
high-voltage AC from the power grid (ranging from 13.8-34.5kVAC) is converted into DC, 2) Isolation stage: voltage
is reduced (by converting the DC back into very high-frequency AC, passing it through a tiny transformer and
converting it back to DC) and galvanic isolation is provided (preventing dangerous electrical shocks or short circuits)
and 3) Output stage: final power is outputted as 800VDC.

Advantages of SSTs. SSTs are viewed as critical enablers for 800VDC data centers, especially as the power density
needs increase. Importantly, as power systems are increasing in complexity, there is a growing focus on leveraging
equipment with more advanced controls, better efficiencies, and greater compatibility with renewable energy,
rather than simply increasing or decreasing voltage levels. While SSTs maintain similar efficiency levels as traditional
transformers (~98%-99%+) under normal conditions, SSTs outperform when there are variable or partial load
conditions, which is very relevant to AI training and inference workloads. Additionally, since SSTs are 50% smaller
and lighter than traditional transformers, they not only free up space for compute hardware, but they can also sit
closer to the actual data center rack, reducing redundant AC-to-DC conversion stages, which minimizes energy loss
and improves overall efficiencies.

Disadvantages of SSTs. A primary drawback of SSTs is the higher initial cost compared with traditional transformers.
Based on market data, our Clean Energy team sees SSTs at c.5-10x the cost of a traditional transformer, and, during
a recent expert webcast discussing 800VDC (see here), current SST pricing was indicated at c.$400-500k per MW.
However, as companies continue to advance capabilities around SSTs and production capacity increases, this can
help reduce costs, making them more affordable. Additionally, as data center power requirements are expected to
step up in the coming years, the power conversion loss associated with traditional architecture will become more
extreme and much more costly. While SSTs entail meaningfully higher unit costs compared with traditional
transformers, they offer the potential to reduce the total cost of ownership for data centers.

Global SST market may reach up to $5bn in 2030E
Leveraging our GS Sustain team's forecasts, we estimate c.10GW of new data center capacity using 800V GPUs
in 2030 (c.6% of the installed base and c.60% of new additions in 2030E). This equates to a revenue
opportunity from SSTs as high as ~$5bn, assuming various pricing levels for the technology. We note the early
stage juncture of this opportunity implies that market sizing will evolve as visibility improves and products
start to move into pilot stage, likely in 2027.

What is the opportunity and potential timing? In aggregate, the global transformer market is estimated at ~$65bn
per year. Infineon has characterized the SST market as having an expected market value of more than $1bn in 2030,
which compares with the conventional transformer market of more than $15bn. Our industry checks indicate that
SSTs can have power capacities of 1MW-10MW, providing capabilities to power multiple server racks. As a result, a 1
GW data center could require 100-1,000 SSTs, although we believe larger data centers would likely be utilizing larger
SSTs. Additionally, data centers will likely build in some redundancy in case there is an issue with one or more of the
SSTs, with a typical build potentially requiring 110%-130% of the required capacity.

At a price of ~$100,000-$350,000/MW per SST (reflecting expected cost deflation and manufacturing scale
relative to current pilot pricing), this equates to a ~$110mn-$450mn opportunity per 1 GW data center. We
note that our SUSTAIN team estimates that between 2028 and 2030, there will be 37 GW of data center
deployments globally, and we calculate that 32 GW should be derived from Blackwell/Rubin/Feynman/other GPUs
that can leverage the 800V opportunity. As a result, we estimate the 800V market as offering ~$3bn-$14bn in total
market potential for SSTs between 2028 and 2030 depending on pricing. Specific to 2030, based on the SUSTAIN
team's forecast, we see ~10 GW of global data centers leveraging 800V GPUs, with this representing a
~$1bn-$5bn annual market opportunity depending on where pricing shakes out. We note that these estimates
include both Blackwell servers (which our Clean Energy team suggests are compatible with 800VDC
architectures) and Rubin servers. Were we to include only Rubin servers, this would imply c.7GW of new data
center capacity using 800V GPUs in 2030 (c.4% of installed base and c.40% of new additions in 2030). Applying
similar logic to solid state circuit breakers, which, per our DC expert call (here), is estimated to cost c.$600k per MW
(5x the price of current circuit breakers), we see a potential TAM of $5-8bn in 2030E.

Other potential markets for SSTs. We highlight that these estimates are solely representative of the data center
market. However, given the ability for SSTs to operate at high voltages as well as high frequencies, they are being
pursued for other applications such as EV fast-charging, renewable integration (solar and wind), railway systems and
transportation, and broader grid modernization. As a result, there is likely upside to these estimates based on the
market penetration within these other verticals.

items.name: TPCA 2026 quick takeaways - 大尺寸、高層數、整合多顆內埋Bridge _ 矽電容、多層芯板.pdf
items.text:
台灣股市｜科技

                                                                             事件分析


Fubon Research                     TPCA 2026 quick takeaways
2026 年 10 月 20 日

                                   大尺寸、高層數、整合多顆內埋 Bridge / 矽電容、多層芯板
                                    1.高階載板:大尺寸、高層數、整合內埋元件（Bridge / 矽電容）
                                                                      、多層芯板
                                    2. EMIB-T 載板需極高對位精度
                                    3. CPO（Co-Packaged Optics）IC 載板扮演著極關鍵的高密度整合平台角色


                                   高階載板: 大尺寸、高層數、整合多顆內埋元件（Bridge / 矽電容）
                                                                      、多層芯板
                                   AI 資料中心持續提升運算效能，主要面臨高速互連、高效供電及熱管理三大技術挑
                                   戰，隨著晶片整合規模擴大、功耗增加，PCB 與 IC 載板必須朝更大尺寸、更高密度
                                   及更多層數發展，並同步提升訊號完整性、電源完整性及翹曲控制能力。隨著 AI
資料來源: TPCA                         GPU、CPO（光電共封裝）與高階 Networking Switch（網路交換器）的晶片尺寸
                                   與功耗爆發，載板尺寸正朝向「極大尺寸（Extreme Large Body Size）
                                                                             」發展。極
                                   大尺寸必須搭配加厚的 Multi-Layer Core（如 2 層、3 層至 6 層 Core）
                                                                                  ，以提供
                                   足夠的結構剛性。整合多顆內埋元件（Bridge / 矽電容）可進一步化電源與訊號完
                                   整性。先進封裝及伺服器系統加速升級，也對 IC 載板提出更高技術要求。


                                   載板尺寸正朝向「極大尺寸（Extreme Large Body Size）
                                                                       」發展。
                                   在高階載板（IC Substrates）產業中，隨著 AI GPU、CPO（光電共封裝）與高階
                                   Networking Switch（網路交換器）的晶片尺寸與功耗爆發，Body Size（載板尺寸）
                                   正朝向「極大尺寸（Extreme Large Body Size）
                                                                   」發展。過去 100 x 100 mm 即被
                                   視為極大尺寸；目前業界已進入 110 x 110 mm 量產階段，並推進至 150 x 130
                                   mm 與 150 x 150 mm（如 CPO 載板）的樣品開發與驗證階段。針對未來高效能
                                   Switch 與 CPO 產品，載板尺寸已進一步升級至 230 x 230 mm 的極限規格。當
黃韻庭                                尺寸擴大至 100 x 100 mm 以上時，載板總層數普遍達到 15~20 層以上；若推
yunting.huang@fubon.com            進至 230 x 230 mm，整體結構更需要高達 30 多層（如 16 + 2 + 16）
                                                                                。極大尺
886-2-27815995#37117
                                   寸必須搭配加厚的 Multi-Layer Core（如 2 層、3 層至 6 層 Core）
                                                                                ，以提供足夠
                                   的結構剛性，並增設電源/接地層（Power/Ground）以維護電源完整性（PI）
                                                                           。在大
李耿聿
aaron.gy.li@fubon.com              尺寸載板上，業界不再追求極端微細線路。因為面積足夠容納線路，過細過密的線
886-2-27815995#37107               路反而容易引發訊號干擾；研發重心已轉向「大尺寸、高層數、整合多顆內埋元件
                                   （Bridge / 矽電容）
                                                」。


                                    圖表 1: IC substrate , EBS( extreme large body size)


                                   資料來源: Unimicron


SMCSee last page for disclaimer.                                                         1
                                                                            台灣股市｜科技

                                                                           事件分析


                                   Advanced substrate - Embedded Passive 埋入式被動元件載板
                                   1)因應高功耗需求：隨著 AI GPU 等高算力晶片的功耗與用電量急劇增加，晶片需
                                   要更龐大且穩定的電力供應; 2)大幅縮短傳輸距離：傳統設計中，電源需由載板最底
                                   層走較長的路徑傳遞至上層晶片；埋入矽電容後，電能可預先儲存在電容中並近距
                                   離直接供電，傳輸路徑顯著縮短 以及 3)優化電源與訊號完整性：近距離供電能有
                                   效提供更穩定的電源供應，優化 Power Integrity（PI，電源完整性） 與 Signal
                                   Integrity（SI，訊號完整性），促進電訊號傳遞。IC substrate (Flip Chip BGA)
                                   Embedded Passive 可改善電源完整性（PI）與縮短供電路徑。矽電容主要埋設於
                                   載板的增層（Build-up layer）結構中。位置偏向接近載板最上層，以便最直接地為
                                   上方晶片提供電力支援。Roadmap 顯示 2026 量產結構為 10/2/10; 8/6/8，NPI 為
                                   18/2/18; 10/n/10，2027 為 14/n/14，2028 為 16/n/16，最大板身從 93x93mm
                                   成長至 150x150mm。


                                    圖表 2: IC substrate ,Embedded passive


                                   資料來源: Unimicron


                                   EMIB-T 載板需極高對位精度
                                   Bridge / Interposer（矽橋/中介層）埋入載板內部以提升晶片間傳輸效率。主要技
                                   術門檻: 1) 極高對位精度（Alignment）
                                                           ：放置 Bridge 等微小元件時，必須精確與
                                   上下層的微細線路及盲孔（Via）對齊，對位稍有偏差即失效。2)異材質結合與可靠
                                   度（Material Bonding & Reliability）
                                                                   ：矽元件與載板有機材料間的接合面容易產生
                                   氣泡，在後續熱驗證中易引發分層（Delamination）問題。3)不可重工（No Rework）
                                   與高成本：元件一旦埋入便無法取出一重工；若對位或接合不良導致瑕疵，整塊
                                   Panel/載板即宣告報廢，產生極高的成本風險; 4) 事前檢測（Known Good Die,
                                   KGD）
                                      ：為避免將不良元件埋入導致載板報廢，元件在嵌入前必須先通過嚴格的良率
                                   檢測。5)多顆矽橋（Multi-Bridge）倍增的良率挑戰:隨著高階晶片尺寸（Body Size）
                                                                                    ，
                                   載板內部需要同時內埋多顆 Bridge 元件。多顆內埋使對位與結合難度呈倍數級上
                                   升。


SMCSee last page for disclaimer.                                                              2
                                                                            台灣股市｜科技

                                                                           事件分析


                                   Multi-Layer Core（多層芯板 / 多層 Core） 載板
                                   為高階載板（IC Substrate）為因應高效能運算與 AI 晶片需求所採用的核心結構
                                   技術。與傳統單一大塊單層 Core 的設計不同，Multi-Layer Core 是將兩層、三層
                                   或更多層的 Core（C）
                                               ，中間透過 PP（Prepreg，半固化片） 黏合疊加在一起，使
                                   載板中間的芯板結構顯著加厚。Multi-Layer Core（多層芯板 / 多層 Core） 載板
                                   可帶來, 1)電源完整性（PI）與訊號完整性（SI）
                                                            ：因應 AI GPU 與伺服器晶片功耗
                                   及用電量大增，多層 Core 能設置更多 Power / Ground（電源層與接地層） 來分
                                   流電流，為單一晶片提供更穩定充足的電力，優化 PI 與 SI。2) 結構強度與板彎控
                                   制（Warping & Planarity）
                                                        ：加厚的 Core 結構能提升整體載板的剛性與平整度，
                                   協助抵御熱應力與板彎形變。雖然市場曾討論「Core 變厚是否需轉用 Glass Core」
                                                                               ，
                                   但 Glass Core 現階段面臨易碎、價格高昂且缺乏成熟量產供應鏈的限制，因此現
                                   階段高階載板仍以 Multi-Layer Core 的有機材料疊合方案為主。


                                    圖表 3: IC substrate, Multi-layer core


                                   資料來源: Unimicron


                                   CPO（Co-Packaged Optics）IC 載板扮演著極關鍵的高密度整合平台角色
                                   由於 CPO 載板周邊需要配置光學模組與多種週邊零件，導致其 Body Size（載板
                                   尺寸）比一般 GPU 載板更大，且趨勢是越做越大。目前 CPO 載板正積極推進至
                                   150 x 150 mm（目前多處於開發與送樣驗證階段）；未來針對高階 Networking
                                   Switch，尺寸更可延伸至 230 x 230 mm 的極限規格。配合大尺寸設計，CPO 載
                                   板的層數普遍落在 15~20 層以上（甚至高達 20 幾層至 30 幾層）
                                                                       。CPO 載板集
                                   成了極大尺寸（Large Body Size）
                                                         、多層芯板（Multi-Layer Core）
                                                                               、微孔（Micro
                                   Via）以及內埋元件（Embedded Bridge / 矽電容）等多項高階技術。雖然光學連
                                   接器型態可能改變，但載板本身依然不可或缺，持續作為晶片與光電模組間供電與
                                   訊號承載的核心基底。


SMCSee last page for disclaimer.                                                       3
                                                                            台灣股市｜科技

                                                                           事件分析


                                    圖表 4:IC substrate, CPO (Co-package optics)


                                   資料來源: Unimicron

 2.   2Q26 毛利率落底，3Q26 起產品組合將顯著改善
     台表科 9 月營收 51.6 億元（+11.5%MoM， +15.9%YoY），
     主要受惠 DDR5、美系手機客戶、美系車用客戶相關產品出
     貨增加，以及部分客戶提前拉貨。3Q26 整體營收 144.6 億
     元（+9.3%QoQ，+13.1%YoY），營收達成率 104%，優於公司
     原先預期 +5%QoQ。推估 3Q26 產品組合為 Display 45%、
     Mini LED 11%、Cable 7%、Auto 10%、DDR5 15%、Touch 5%、
     Others（新應用）7%。
     2Q26 受 LCD 出貨比重增加導致產品組合較差，加上 2Q26
     提前備料使原材料庫存成本先行反映，使得毛利率 11.8%，
     低於原先預估 12.8%。展望 3Q26，部分產品新報價將開始
     反應，同時 DDR5 因 PCB、PMIC 等材料供應緊張，部分訂
     單 改採 不 帶 料商 業 模 式 ， 因 此儘 管 DDR5 營收僅 成 長
     +5%YoY，出貨量仍高達+30%QoQ，毛利率與毛利仍將優於不
     帶料模式。同時消費性產品占比下降，記憶體與車用等高
     毛利產品增加，研究部預期 3Q26 毛利率仍有望達 14.1%
     （+2.3ppts QoQ，+1.5ppts YoY），較前一季明顯改善，預
     期 3Q26 稅後 EPS 維持 3.50 元。


3.   傳統消費產品受供需環境雙面夾擊，未來成長來自非消費性
     公司過去主要以消費性產品為主，包含 T-CON、Display
     Control Board、Light Bar、Mini LED 背光板及 Touchpad
     等，終端應用涵蓋 TV、Monitor、NB 及 Apple 相關產品。
     展望未來，消費性需求仍相對疲弱，中系面板客戶面臨終端
     需求不振、面板售價難以調漲，以及 PCB、CCL 等原材料成
     本上升壓力，預期傳統消費性業務持續衰退。惟美系客戶 NB
     需求良好，日、韓系客戶近年陸續導入新產品，受惠低基期
     及新訂單貢獻，此部分預期 2027 年仍可維持成長，抵銷中
     系及其他傳統客戶需求下滑，整體而言，研究部仍保守預期
     2027 年顯示業務維持個位數衰退，長期營收佔比將逐漸下
     降。


                        請參見末頁重要批露及免責聲明              2
 4.   AI 高速擴張使得長期前段 SMT 外包需求將大幅增加
     近年終端 AI 應用高速發展，相關供應鏈均大幅擴廠，進而排
     擠其他應用的供給。上下游供應鏈不斷上修資本支出，持續
     出現漲價通知均表示嚴重供不應求。PCBA 需求量應與 PCB 需
     求高度相關，Prismark 預估近年 PCB 產值受到 AI 需求帶動
     價與量的成長。研究部認為供應鏈將優先將資源放在後段產
     能擴張，原先客戶 In-house 的前段 PCBA 將成為下階段供不
     應求的資源，前段 SMT 外包需求有望大幅增加，以降低資本
     投入、縮短擴產時間並提高生產彈性。隨新應用放量，自有
     與外包產能不足，使得台表科有機會接觸更多潛在客戶，長
     期同步受惠價與量的成長。

     台表科競爭優勢主要來自三方面：1. 公司具備約 240 條
     SMT 產線及大規模量產經驗，可依不同產品需求彈性調整
     設備配置，相較小型 SMT 代工廠更有能力快速承接大量訂
     單。2. 公司生產據點涵蓋中國、台灣、越南、印度及墨西
     哥，非中產能布局有利因應美系 CSP 供應鏈去中化、製造
     地分散的需求。3. 公司長期專注高精度 SMT 打件，相較
     傳統 TFT-LCD，新應用產品具備更高的元件密度與高速訊
     號完整性要求，對打件定位精度、PCB 翹曲控制、焊點品質
     及製程一致性要求更加嚴格。針對不同製程站點需強化
     Particle 污染控制，並增加 AOI、X-ray 等檢測設備及品
     質檢查程序，以降低微小異物、焊接缺陷及組裝偏差對後續
     光電測試良率與可靠度的影響。不同客戶也存在不同封裝、
     來料與製程安排，需要持續調整設備參數、治具及檢驗流
     程，因此並非傳統 SMT 產線可直接轉換。


                               請參見末頁重要批露及免責聲明                         3
      光通訊產線投資金額約為傳統 TFT-LCD 2–3 倍，傳輸速
     度的升級對設備調整與資金投入亦有雙位數的成長。高階
     製程經驗、客戶認證及量產能力使得公司具有一定護城河，
     較有機會在客戶擴張時享有主要供應商的資格，先行取得
     高加工單價。


5.   受惠 AI 記憶體需求激增，DDR5 與客戶擴產一同成長
     台表科 2018 年即開始接洽美系與中系記憶體客戶。由記
     憶體廠提供 DRAM 顆粒，公司主要負責封裝完成後的 DRAM
     IC、PMIC 等零組件 SMT 打件、回焊及相關檢測。公司藉由
     長期累積的 SMT 製程與良率管理能力、大規模產線及彈性
     調度能力，在過去已通過記憶體客戶與終端 CSP 客戶認
     證，使得客戶放心將所有後段 SMT 模組製程委外交由台表
     科。
     過去 DRAM 產業景氣循環波動較大，2022–2023 年因庫存
     修正及價格下跌，記憶體廠商減少資本支出與生產活動。
     2024 年後隨 AI Data Center 快速擴張，HBM 與 DDR5 需
     求同步增加，一方面 HBM 占用大量先進 DRAM 晶圓資源，
     間接使一般 DRAM 供給趨緊；另一方面 AI Server 的 CPU
     記憶體需求直接推升 DDR5 RDIMM 出貨，帶動模組 SMT 需
     求成長。
     展望未來，公司記憶體業務主要與客戶擴產同步成長。台
     表科自 2025 年起記憶體業務成長動能逐步增強，2026 年
     中系記憶體出貨量預估成長 +50%YoY，2027 年再成長
     +30–50%YoY。公司亦規劃於 4Q26 新增 4 條產線，預估
     1Q27 記憶體產能有望提升 20–30%。美系客戶自 9 月起
     訂單亦逐步增加。
     由於 PCB、PMIC、MLCC 等零組件供應吃緊，短期出貨仍受
     料況限制，未來部分訂單將改採不帶料模式，可降低營運
     資金需求，同時不帶料模式加上稼動率提升，儘管營收成
     長受影響，毛利率與毛利絕對值仍有望大幅提升。

6.   光通訊產品放量提前，4Q26 佔比明顯提升
     台表科目前光通訊訂單來自原一位美系光通訊客戶，原先
     預期 2H26 放量 800G、2Q27 試產 1.6T 並於 2H27 放
     量。而近期客戶需求明顯優於預期，目前 800G 已開始放
     量，1.6T 更提前至 3Q26 試產，4Q26 開始少量交貨。相
     較 100G、400G，800G、1.6T 具備更高製程精度及代工單
     價，有望提升產品組合。儘管部分出貨瓶頸來自 PCB 等零
     組件料況，研究部仍預期 4Q26 此位美系客戶營收占比有
     望達 4–5%，1Q27 持續提升至 4Q27 達 8–10%。
     除既有美系客戶持續放量外，目前已確定 2027 年將新增
     一位美系客戶，同時公司正接洽另一美系與中系光通訊客
     戶。近期美國加強中國光收發模組供應鏈安全審查，美系
     CSP 對非中產能及零組件來源要求提高，促使中系光模組
     廠更有誘因將前段 PCBA／SMT 製程委外至海外。台表科具
     備台灣、越南及墨西哥等非中生產據點，相較中國 SMT 廠
     更有機會符合部分美系客戶的產地要求，成為爭取新增訂
     單的重要競爭優勢。預期光通訊廠將專注於後段擴產，加
     上政策趨勢影響，委外比例有望持續提升，新客戶規模均
     遠大於原美系客戶，公司光通訊業務將進一步擴張，預估
     2027 年底光通訊營收占比有望達 20%。

7.    AI Server、衛星及機器人新應用持續拓展
     （1） 台表科持續承接台系 ODM、美系 EMS 及其他客戶 AI
         Server SMT 外溢訂單，主要受惠 AI Data Center 建
         置需求強勁，既有系統廠與 ODM 產能優先供應大型客
         戶，使部分 PCBA 訂單轉向專業 SMT 代工廠。目前公
         司以 Power Board、BBU 及其他小型板件為主，多採
         客戶供料的純代工模式，並逐步洽談 Server 主板及
         連工帶料訂單，預計 2027 年開始導入較高價值的大
         型板件。目前 AI Server 營收占比約 2%，預期 2027
         年提升逾 5%。


                                     請參見末頁重要批露及免責聲明                            6
      （2） 針對美系車用客戶，公司已供應車門把手、Display、
         Camera Module 及相關電子板件，2H26 出貨逐步增
         加，同時客戶合作範圍由傳統車用逐步擴大，2027 年
         將延伸切入 Robot Camera Module、地面衛星、客戶自
         用 Data Center Power Board。公司已參與地面衛星
         相關板件代工，衛星端產品則因可靠度及測試要求較
         高，仍處導入與試產階段，預計 4Q26 開始少量出貨，
         2027 年逐步放量。公司亦布局美系客戶機器人關節控
         制 PCBA 等應用，相關產品預期於 2027 年進入量產，
         初期貢獻低個位數佔比。


8.    因應新應用需求，26-27 年資本支出大幅上修
      台表科過去產能主要集中於中國，約占整體 SMT 產線
      82%，近年隨美系客戶供應鏈去中化及新應用需求增加，公
      司持續擴充台灣、越南、印度及墨西哥等海外據點。因應中
      系記憶體客戶需求，2026 年規劃中國合肥將新增五條 SMT
      線，其中一條已於年初開始貢獻，其餘四條預計 1Q27 投
      產，帶動 2027 年產能提升 30%；印度廠則持續擴充記憶體
      模組及網通相關產能，預計 2H27 增加美系記憶體客戶供
      貨；越南為未來光通訊及 AI Data Center 主要擴產基地，
      二期廠房預計 1Q27 完工，後續三期仍具擴充空間以因應
      新增美系光通訊客戶需求；墨西哥廠規劃再增加 2–3 條
      SMT 線，主要供應 Data Center 與車用產品。此外，部分
      美系客戶對美國在地製造具有需求，公司亦評估美國設廠
      可行性，惟仍須視客戶訂單規模及投資效益決定。
      公司 SMT 產線由 2024 年約 230 條提升至 2025–2026
      年約 240 條，預計 2027 年將超過 250 條，公司自 2025
      年重新進入擴產週期，預期 2026 年 CapEx 由原先預估
      US$150mn 持續上修至 US$180mn，2027 年 CapEx 也將超
      過 US$150mn，投資重心由廠房土建逐步轉向生產設備。

9.   27 年高毛利非顯示佔比將近五成
     展望未來，台表科傳統消費電子業務受終端需求疲弱、面
     板報價及原材料成本壓力影響，整體 Display 營收恐面臨
     衰退，惟美系客戶、日韓系新客戶、Mini LED 仍有望維持
     成長。未來成長動能將由傳統顯示應用轉向記憶體、光通
     訊、AI Server 等新應用，帶動公司產品組合與獲利結構明
     顯改善。綜上所述，預估 2026/2027 年營收從 544/646 億
     元上修至 550/705 億元（+10.5/+28.0%YoY），預期 2025-

     年 提 升 ， 預 期    2025-2027    年 毛 利 率 分 別 為

通用人工智慧(AGI)時代來臨
  -AI 從模型競賽進入代理人時代
  -相關的運算基礎設施投資機會


                        黃鵬睿
                     10/16/2026

群益投顧
                9月OpenAI推出GPT-6 Astra
 ⚫   OpenAI 9月推出GPT-6 Astra，該模型由逾10萬顆Grace Blackwell晶片訓練
     而成。是OpenAI規模最大的一次訓練成果。
 ⚫   GPT-6 Astra 是 OpenAI 目前旗下能力最強的前沿旗艦模型。它具備頂級的
     複雜邏輯推理、軟體工程（Codex）、科學研究與電腦操作能力。Astra能
     在軟體中直接操作，包括排版法律合約、開發3D遊戲、依表格填寫報稅草
     稿等。OpenAI總裁Greg Brockman表示，未來回顧或許Astra會被視為AGI
     誕生時刻，留待使用者判斷。執行長Sam Altman稱Astra推出時程比預期長，
     交由川普政府正式審查後才發布，期望AI帶動創業、創新與經濟成長熱潮。
 ⚫   AGI當前未有統一標準，OpenAI認為AGI可定義爲在多數具經濟價值的工
     作上，表現超出人類的高度自主系統。


資料來源：電子時報、群益投顧彙整
群益投顧                        2
             9月底OpenAI DevDay，Dots亮相
 ⚫   在9月底的開發者大會上，OpenAI發表可全天候執行任務的Dots代理、新
     模型GPT-6.1 Sol，以及團隊協作平台ChatGPT Space。有別於過去的聊天機
     器人，Dots 擁有獨立的雲端電腦，可串接超過 4,000 個第三方應用程式。
     它能作為「虛擬員工」在背景自主推進長週期的跨平台任務（如程式碼除
     錯、專案追蹤、資訊彙整與自動化排程），並透過主流通訊軟體溝通。
     GPT-6 Astra則是Dots的驅動模型。GPT-6.1 Sol則是Astra 低成本、但能力相
     近的版本，性價比高，希望緩解算力成本高的挑戰。
 ⚫   本次發表最大的亮點仍是Dots，OpenAI挾先發優勢與龐大的開發者社群，
     透過專屬雲端電腦環境與超過 4,000 個第三方應用程式的 API 深度綁定，
     企圖打造出類似 iOS 的 Agent 閉環生態系，將企業與個人的工作流牢牢鎖
     在 OpenAI 的基礎設施內。
 ⚫   預計下一步，AI 代理將以實體裝置出現，OpenAI預期最快2027年發表


資料來源：電子時報、群益投顧彙整

群益投顧                        3
                 同月Meta加入代理式AI戰局
 ⚫   Meta 也於9月推出Muse在蘋果美國App Store上架後，Sensor Tower資料顯
     示，6天內下載量累計超過90.2萬次，超越Meta AI App同期的約77萬次。
 ⚫   Muse可以幫使用者規劃並完成日常瑣事，例如發送email、更改機票等。
     Meta強調，用戶無需學習就可以上手使用Muse，可說是無任何技術門檻，
     就能打造個人化的AI助理。
 ⚫   這 揭 示 AI 代 理 的 發 展 越 趨 成 熟 。 隨 問 答 式 聊 天 機 器 人 、 生 成 式 AI
     （Generative AI）轉向自主執行型代理，OpenAI、Google、Anthropic、
     Perplexity、SpaceXAI等科技大廠皆進一步推出AI代理服務，其載體各異，
     涵蓋雲端虛擬機、瀏覽器、本機沙盒等路線，皆強調能協助不同領域的工
     作，如業務、行銷、財務、人資、社群等。

 群益投顧                         5
                目前主要AI代理與功能


資料來源：電子時報、群益投顧彙整
群益投顧               6
                AI代理揭示基礎建設發展路徑
 ⚫   1.推論算力進入爆發期。AI 代理將算力消耗模式轉化為「機器對機器」的
     24 小時連續運算。處理複合任務時，涉及目標拆解、反思糾錯、多步驟工
     具調用與長文本上下文維持，其推論端的 FLOPs 消耗量呈現幾何級數放大。
 ⚫   2.雲端重型推論（Heavy Cloud）與端雲協同（Edge/Hybrid）並行。應用
     不再由單一龐大模型通吃，而是出現明確的架構分層：
      ⚫ B2B / 企業工作流（Dots 代表）： 追求頂級邏輯推理能力，依賴雲端極致算力
        （如 GPT-6 Astra）與雲端虛擬電腦環境，透過高客單價訂閱與 API 實現商業
        變現。
      ⚫ B2C / 消費端日常（Muse 代表）： 追求低延遲、隱私與環境感知，走向「端
        雲協同＋邊緣記憶」模式，透過硬體配件與手機本地端運算整合，形成高黏著
        度的生態閉環。代表算力需求從資料中心延伸至具備 NPU 的邊緣運算晶片。
 ⚫   3.資料傳輸頻寬與互連成為首要瓶頸。代理執行複雜流程時，任務調度高
     度依賴 CPU、GPU 與 ASIC 晶片的異質協同運算。晶片內與晶片間頻繁的
     資料交換，使得「記憶體牆（Memory Wall）」與「I/O 頻寬傳輸延遲」成
     為系統效率的最大掣肘。純算力堆疊的邊際效益遞減，先進封裝、光通訊
     傳輸以及高速網路介面晶片的戰略價值因此顯著拉升。
資料來源：公司財報、群益投顧彙整
群益投顧                      7
                      AI代理時代受惠股出列


資料來源：Gemini、群益投顧彙整
 群益投顧                   8
            新思、益華提高預期、導入AI代理
 ⚫   AI 代理需要跨軟體、多步驟自主推理時，通用晶片性價比遞減，ASIC與
     Chiplet架構加速發展。新思與益華本質是高毛利、高黏著度的專利軟體
     訂閱制。晶片越複雜、設計週期越長，EDA 授權金與 IP 權利金多。益華
     近期上修2026全年財測、新思也維持2027年營收獲利高成長的預期。
 ⚫   新思(10/2026)的投資者日上，提出3種代理式AI導入方式，包括部署完整
     的Synopsys Autopilot平台、將新思代理整合進客戶自有AI平台，以及使
     用針對特定工程流程最佳化的前瞻模型，收費方式結合訂閱制與用量計
     費。未來新思針對同一個客戶，可以在設計階段支付工具訂閱與用量費
     用，導入IP時支付授權與客製化費用，量產後再支付權利金，整段流程
     可以有更多獲利的機會。
 ⚫   益華則推出AI超級代理平台AuraStack。工程師未來只需以自然語言描述
     設計目標、成本限制與效能需求，AuraStack便能自動調用Cadence既有
     EDA工具鏈，完成元件選擇、電路布局、封裝規畫、模擬驗證與虛擬測
     試等工作流程，將產品上市時間縮短約50%，部分設計任務的生產力甚
     至可提升15倍。輝達、台積電與施耐德電機為AuraStack早期使用者。

 群益投顧                    10
                   ARM發揮空間也大幅上升
 ⚫   ARM 過去只賣 IP 授權與架構指令集，按晶片平均售價抽取 1.5%~2.5%
     的權利金，研發週期長且附加價值被晶片設計業者（如高通、聯發科）
     拿走大半。ARM 現在直接為雲端客戶提供「預先驗證、完成物理佈局」
     的運算子系統（CSS）。這將客戶設計一款先進伺服器 CPU 的時間從兩
     年縮短至數月。且能向 CSP 抽取數倍於傳統架構的權利金費率。
 ⚫   無論是端點個人代理人硬體，還是雲端資料中心的推論叢集，ARM 的低
     功耗架構都有優勢。隨著最新 v9 架構（ARM最新的晶片設計藍圖）的專
     利費率翻倍，加上 Neoverse 雲端處理器（ARM 雲端資料中心、伺服器與
     基礎設施IP）在雲端服務商自研晶片中的滲透率不斷提高，ARM 正在享
     受邊緣與雲端推論的雙重權利金紅利。
 ⚫   微軟、亞馬遜、Meta 越想繞過 Nvidia，就越依賴新思、益華與ARM。軟
     體巨頭缺乏傳統半導體公司的龐大設計團隊，因此他們必採用 ARM 的
     Neoverse CSS 架構做為核心基礎。大量採購新思、益華預先驗證的高速
     介面 IP，導入其 AI 驅動的設計工具，以演算法自主優化晶片的 PPA（效
     能、功耗、面積）。

                 博通、邁威爾維持主導地位
 ⚫   在傳輸領域仍持續看好博通、邁威爾。博通是全球高速乙太網路晶片與
     PCIe 6.0 交換技術的領導者，完全定義資料中心集群傳輸的標準。另外，
     它是科技巨頭自研 AI 晶片（ASIC）的最大幕後推手。CSP 多數沒有底
     層的網通設計能力，必須仰賴博通的 ASIC 委託設計與高速介面 IP 整合。
 ⚫   邁威爾在10/6投資者日上明確指出，AI 工作負載正超越傳統的訓練，正
     式邁入「推理模型與 Agentic AI」的規模化階段。轉變帶來龐大的資料移
     動需求。邁威爾將 2028 財年的營收指引，從 180 億美元上調至約 200 億
     美元。到2031財年，預估總潛在市場（TAM）將高達約 4,000 億美元，
     並喊出 2031 財年營收將達到 700 至 900 億美元的區間，中值800億美元，
     遠高於市場原先預估的470億美元。
 ⚫   新增成長主要來自資料中心連接產品需求，包括交換器晶片、scale-up互
     連與光學元件，用於AI伺服器內部及不同機櫃、叢集之間的大量資料傳
     輸。AI模型訓練與推論使用的加速器數量持續增加，資料中心對高速、
     低延遲互連的需求同步升高，連接能力也逐漸從配套元件，轉變為AI基
     礎設施的核心投資項目。

                 最主要受惠者：AMD、INTC
 ⚫   AI代理依賴大量算力驅動的應用，如今真正主要的兩家算力供應商就是
     AMD和英特爾。隨AI代理在消費端獲得更廣泛採用，在更高強度的推論、
     調度協同及基礎設施工作負載推動下，伺服器CPU需求將有望直接受惠。
 ⚫   Agentic AI 需維持長週期的對話記憶（Dossier）與長文本上下文，並頻繁
     調用 KV Cache，推論架構的核心瓶頸在於記憶體頻寬而非純算力。AMD
     的 Instinct 系列（MI300X、MI325X）憑藉領先的 HBM3e 容量與頻寬規
     格，在運行開源及企業私有化推理模型時展現極高的每代幣成本（Cost-
     per-token）優勢，成為CSP為降低推論成本的替代方案。
 ⚫   Agent 在執行多步驟任務時，大量的邏輯判斷、API 呼叫、工具分發與系
     統 I/O 本質上由 CPU 掌控。AMD EPYC CPU在每瓦效能與核心密度上持
     續獲取市佔，使其能在「EPYC（任務調度與數據前處理）+ Instinct（深
     度推理）」的完整異質推論架構中，同步獲取雙重晶片營收。


資料來源：Bloomberg，群益投顧彙整
 群益投顧                     18
                 最主要受惠者：AMD、INTC
 ⚫   企業部署AI代理最棘手的障礙是內部營運數據與商業機密的合規風險，
     絕大多數企業不能將所有日常工作流全部送至公有雲。Intel 掌握全球超
     過七成的企業商用 PC 與客戶端裝機量（Installed Base），其搭載高算力
     NPU 的 Core Ultra 處理器，正是企業個人 Agent在終端本地 24/7 運行的
     硬體基座。
 ⚫   大量中小企業與傳統產業無法負擔昂貴的 GPU 叢集。Intel Xeon 6 處理器
     具備成熟的 AMX（進階矩陣擴充）加速引擎，能直接以 CPU 叢集運行
     中小型參數量（如 8B 至 70B）的推論模型，在私有雲資料中心內充當成
     本最低、佈署最快的輕量級 Agent 執行中樞。
 ⚫   受惠於代理式AI應用崛起，伺服器CPU也掀起缺貨潮，超微部分產品交
     期已達8~10週，英特爾產品最長更來到6個月，連帶下游伺服器廠商的平
     均交期延長至8~12週以上，帶動客戶積極洽談長期供貨協議（LTA），
     進一步推升CPU供應鏈訂單能見度。


資料來源：Bloomberg，群益投顧彙整
 群益投顧                      19
                         超微半導體(AMD US)


資料來源：Bloomberg，群益投顧彙整
 群益投顧                      20
                         英特爾(INTC US)


資料來源：Bloomberg，群益投顧彙整
 群益投顧                      21
                         大贏家：台積電
 ⚫   過去模型訓練高度集中於 Nvidia 單一架構；但 Agent 時代強調 24 小時不
     間斷運行的「每瓦效能比」與「總擁有成本（TCO）」。這迫使 Google
     （TPU）、Meta（MTIA）、AWS（Trainium）、微軟（Maia）全面加速
     自研客製化推論 ASIC。對台積電而言，CSP 廠與傳統 IC 設計廠競相研
     發專用推論晶片，使投片客戶從「少數晶片巨頭」擴散為「全體科技巨
     頭」。客戶對台積電的依賴度大幅提高，進一步鞏固台積電「以價值為
     基礎」的絕對議價能力。
 ⚫   在10月的最新法說會上，董事長魏哲家將 2026 全年美元營收成長率預估
     由原先的「略高於 40%」正式上修至 約 44%。財務長黃仁昭重申 2026
     全年資本支出維持 600 億至 640 億美元 不變，並明確釋出 「2026～2028
     年的三年資本支出規模將顯著高於過去三年」 的強烈訊號，印證 AI 結構
     性需求至 2028 年仍未見頂。 針對外資關注 2 奈米放量、海外設廠及電價
     上漲對毛利率的壓抑，魏哲家直言台積電「獲利能力沒有天花板」。這
     意味著 2027 年先進製程與先進封裝的晶圓代工報價調漲（市場預期 5%
     ～10% 漲幅）已具備高度客戶共識，足以轉嫁通膨與折舊成本。

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

                                              representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard

Nien Made Enterprise
3Q preview: EPS +13% YoY to NT$6.6;
Better 2H but not yet a turnaround
Reiterate Rating: BUY | PO: 441.00 TWD | Price: 358.50 TWD


3Qe EPS NT$6.6: strong rev and GP offset by opex and FX                                                     20 October 2026

Nien Made is scheduled to report 3Q26 results on 4 Nov. Disclosed monthly sales imply                       Equity
3Q26 revenue growth of 16% YoY to NT$8.5bn, or 9% in USD terms, largely
volume-driven. Growth reaccelerated from 1.7% YoY in 1H26, led by custom-made on a
                                                                                                              Key Changes
low US base and expansion in Europe and Japan. Ready-made also improved as
Cambodia labor shortages eased. (See Exhibit 1 for US window coverings spending                               (NT$)                       Previous      Current

trends). Gross margin: We expect underlying GPM to rise 1.1ppt YoY to 59.8% on lower                          Inv. Opinion                  B-1-8         B-1-7

tariffs, broadly flat QoQ. We forecasts an NT$300mn of IEEPA tariff refunds in 2H26.                          Price Obj.                   425.00        441.00

Assuming NT$150mn is booked in 3Q, this would add 1.7ppt and lift reported GPM to                             2026E EPS                     22.36         22.88

61.5%. We expect the selling expense ratio to fall 1.7ppt QoQ to 17.5% on lower fuel                          2027E EPS                     25.88         25.93

charges, but remain 0.5ppt higher YoY due to continued salesforce and distribution                            2028E EPS                     28.06         28.15

network investment. We expect an FX loss in 3Q26 vs. an NT$118mn gain in 3Q25,
weighing on YoY earnings growth. We forecast 3Q26 EPS of NT$6.6, up 13% YoY.                                Yoyo Pang >>

in Aug-26 for the first time after 19 consecutive months of YoY declines. Spending rose                     Ronald Leung, CFA >>

as normalization off a low base than the start of an industry turnaround. The Aug-Sep

remains a headwind to housing-related demand.                                                               Stock Data

Nien Made Enterprise (XNRBF)
Our PO NT$441 is derived from 17x P/E 2027E EPS. This is around 0.5SD above
historical the one-year forward P/E, which we think is warranted given the visibility of
the growth profile.

Downside risks are 1) weaker-than-expected Home Depot's sell-through, 2) slow
recovery of US housing turnover, and 3) higher tariff increases on China exports to the
US. 4) Loss of key customers.

                                                                                                                      (886) 2 8758 6249
➢ Margin expansion on fast-growing segments (HDI and substrates)                                      thomas.kim@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw


Background: Zhen Ding Technology (ZDT), the world’s largest PCB                                  Share price performance
manufacturer by revenue, generated revenue of TWD182.5bn in 2025.                                  (TWD)                                                      (%)
                                                                                                    650                                                          265
Historically focused on consumer electronics and smartphones, the
company is shifting towards higher-value AI-server PCBs (HLC/iHDI),                                 513                                                          219


optical-module PCBs (mSAP), and IC substrates (ABF/BT). These                                       375                                                          173

businesses accounted for 21.6% of its revenue in 1H26, up from 11.7% in                             238                                                          126

2025. Management targets this ratio to reach c.25% in 2026 and c.30% in                             100                                                          80
2027. To support this shift, ZDT has 22 fabs under construction and plans                             Oct-25      Jan-26        Apr-26        Jul-26
                                                                                                                           Zhen Ding (LHS)
to build nine more, primarily for mSAP/HDI, HLC, and ABF substrates.                                                       Relative to TWSE Index (RHS)


Highlights: ZDT’s “One ZDT strategy” is gradually bearing fruit. Since                           12-month range                                        136.00-646.00
2018, management has pursued its “One ZDT strategy” to broaden the                               Market cap (USDbn)                                            19.05
                                                                                                 3m avg daily turnover (USDm)                                 530.30
product portfolio – including HLC, substrates, mSAP/HDI, rigid-flex and
                                                                                                 Source: FactSet, Daiwa forecasts
SLP – by leveraging its strengths in FPCB and consumer HDI. This
strategy is beginning to pay off, and management expects its fast-growing
segments, including mSAP HDI for optical transceivers, AI-server HDI and
ABF/BT substrates, to gain momentum from this year. Management
expects revenue from these segments to increase by c.150% YoY and
account for c.25% of total revenue (or c.TWD50bn) in 2026, and to further
increase by 100% YoY to TWD100bn in 2027. ZDT targets these fast-
growing segments to reach 30% of its revenue mix in 2027 and c.45-50%
in 2030. Given current progress, the 2030 target could be reached in 2028.
For mSAP HDI, management expects the 800G/1.6T transceiver product
mix to shift to 7:3 in 2027, from 5:5 in 2026, and aims to become the largest
supplier of optical-transceiver HDI in 2027. In AI-server HDI, we expect the
2 leading ASIC vendors to gradually shift from pure HLC to thick HDI
boards – a combination of HLC and HDI – in their next-generation designs,
with ZDT a potential beneficiary. This could drive c.3x growth in ZDT’s
business in 2027.

Product mix to support gross margin expansion. Margin expansion is
increasingly driven by a favourable product mix. Gross margin reached
22.4% in 1H26 (vs. 16.5% in 1H25). Management indicated that optical-
transceiver HDIs currently have the highest gross margin, at over 40%,
followed by IC substrates, with ABF margins potentially reaching 50-60%
and BT margins around 30% as a long-term target. Server HLC margins
are around 20-30%, while HDI margins should be higher given their greater
process complexity. With margins in traditional businesses at c.20%, ZDT
expects growth in the newer segments to drive further margin expansion.

Valuation: The stock is trading at 36/19x PER for 2026/27E based on
Bloomberg consensus. It’s past 3-year PER range is 10-30x.

買進－維持買進

目標價：2,500.0 元　+17.9%
收盤價：2,120.0 元

投資與評價

1. 弘塑 2Q26 毛利率僅達 38.9%，低於我們原先及市場預期的 40%水準，主要受到添鴻產品結構轉差及新廠折舊攤提影響。
2. 3Q26 受惠於 CoWoS 等機台認列數成長及強勁拉貨需求，營收達 22.21 億元；研究部預估 EPS 為 15.86 元。
3. FY26 全年出機量預估維持在 220 至 240 台，展望至 FY27/FY28，FY27 設備出貨量預估將年增 50%，FY28 亦有機會再成長 50%。
4. 研究部預估 FY26/27 EPS 分別為 60.66 元/96.33 元，維持弘塑買進投資建議，目標價 2,500 元，以 26x FY27 獲利估值。

重點更新

至 FY28 出貨量能持續成長

研究部認為弘塑設備出貨展望能見度將能延伸至 FY28。由於晶圓廠、OSAT、記憶體客戶皆對先進封裝設備需求相當迫切，設備交期已長達 10 至 12 個月，惟受限於短期人力供應與廠房備構進度，FY26 全年出機量預估維持在 220 至 240 台，展望至 FY27/FY28，FY27 設備出貨量預估將年增 50%，FY28 亦有機會再成長 50%。

添鴻化學品業務將於 1Q27 逐漸看見轉機

隨 OSAT 客戶於今年 Q2/Q3 進入裝機密集期，新產線仍須經測試與量產爬坡，相關的化學品需求通常會在設備交機後約 3~4 個月逐步提升，因此短期營收仍受新廠折舊與轉動率偏低影響，預期添鴻的整體稼動率與毛利率有望在 1Q27 逐漸擺脫谷底，迎來較為明顯的營運轉機。

訂單能見度無虞

展望 2026 年至 2028 年，在各先進封裝平台強勁需求下，設備產能已告全滿，交期長達 10 至 12 個月，訂單能見度達 2H27，就產品組合來看，設備業務高階產品比重將逐漸提升，預估至 FY27 SoIC/CPO 等營收占比將提升至 10~15%，添鴻化學品也將受惠於 OSAT 客戶逐漸提升拉貨動能，整體營收與獲利成長動能明確。研究部預估 FY26/27 EPS 分別為 60.66 元/96.33 元（YoY +33.5%/+58.8%），弘塑目前交易於 35/22 倍 2026/2027 年獲利預估。研究部維持買進投資建議，目標價 2,500 元，以 26x FY27 獲利估值。
