Supply/Demand Update: Undersupply Deepens in CY27–28
                  Our updated model points to a wider supply shortfall in CY27–28, despite additional
                  capacity: Incorporating the latest expansion plans and semiconductor demand forecasts,
                  we now expect ABF substrate demand to exceed available supply by 9.3% in CY27 and
                  13.7% in CY28, versus 6.2% and 9.4% previously. This represents a widening of 3.1ppt and
                  4.3ppt, respectively, relative to our prior estimates. We maintain our view that CY26 is a
                  broadly balanced market, followed by increasingly tight supply over the next two years.

                  The main demand upgrade comes from other ASICs, including Chinese AI chips: We
                  raise our shipment assumptions for this category to 6.4mn units in CY27 and 8.7mn in
                  CY28, from 4.6mn and 6.2mn previously. Our Nvidia GPU and server CPU forecasts remain
                  largely unchanged, while we lower AMD GPU estimates while also keeping CY27 Trainium
                  and TPU shipments largely unchanged. The tighter substrate outlook therefore reflects
                  stronger demand across a broader set of ASIC suppliers, rather than higher shipment
                  assumptions for every major AI platform. We also raise our substrate content assumptions
                  for select chips based on our latest supply chain checks, lifting our substrate demand
                  estimates across some segments, including server CPUs and networking.

                  Higher supply assumptions provide limited relief in CY27-28: We now include additional
                  capacity announcements that have been announced recently, including two additional
                  Kinsus factories, scheduled to come online in CY28 and CY29, beyond the CY27 expansion
                  already in our model. Several larger projects, however, contribute later. NYPCB’s new site
                  starts ramping in 2H29, while SEMCO’s Sejong expansion begins mass production in
                  September 2028 and its project in Vietnam is scheduled to begin operations by June
                  2030. These additions increase medium-term supply but do not prevent the modeled
                  shortfall from worsening through CY28.

                  Increasing substrate complexity adds to the pressure on usable output: Larger body
                  sizes, higher layer counts, and more demanding manufacturing processes constrain the
                  output available to meet demand, even as suppliers expand installed capacity. With the
                  supply gap widening in CY27-28, we expect tightness to become a more important pricing
                  driver than raw material cost pass-through. This supports our forecast for 25%+ price
                  increases in CY27 and further increases in CY28, alongside continued margin expansion.

    NYPCB (8046.TW, OW, covered by Howard Kao)

    On August 6, NYPCB announced that its Board of Directors had approved a capex budget
    of NT$46.8bn (~US$1,474mn) to invest in building a new ABF substrate production site.
    Our checks indicate that this production site is located in the southern part of Taiwan, and
    will start to ramp up production in 2H29. Given the size of this investment, we estimate
    that it will approximately double its capacity exiting CY30, relative to its CY28 capacity.

    Kinsus (3189.TW, Not Covered)

    In our previous model, we had assumed only one factory (k6b) coming online in CY27,
    increasing capacity ~30%. However, recent checks suggest that Kinsus intends to bring
    two more factories online, one in CY28 (k6c) and one in CY29 (k6d). This implies that
    capacity would increase another ~25% in CY28 and ~20% in CY29, bringing Kinsus' total
    ABF substrate capacity to almost double exiting CY29, relative to its CY26 capacity.

    Ibiden (4062.T, covered by Shoji Sato)

    Back in February, Ibiden first announced that it will invest capex of ¥500bn in the
    electronics field planned through F3/29, for ABF substrate expansion. Sato-san's latest
    view is that Ibiden will need a new factory building to install the equipment and facilities
    that will be purchased with the ¥500bn. As a result, Sato-san expects Ibiden during its 2Q
    results briefing (October 30) to announce plans to make a large capital investment,
    including for a factory building with a long lead time, and raise its medium-term earnings
    forecast (report here).

    SEMCO (009150.KS, covered by Shawn Kim)

    On September 29, SEMCO announced investment of KRW4.27 trillion (~US$3,178mn) in
    Sejong and KRW2.51 trillion (~US$1,488mn) in Vietnam, for AI server semiconductor
    substrate capacity expansion.

        • Sejong: Investment period from September 2026 to May 2028, with mass
           production starting in September 2028. Largest single-product investment to date,
           serving as key hub for mass production of high-value-added, highly demanding
           products, proactively responding to the increasing demand for AI server substrates.
        • Vietnam: The Vietnamese subsidiary aims to complete construction and begin
           operations by June 2030. It will be operated as a strategic hub to respond to global
           volume demand and enhance production efficiency through a stable supply
           system.


    With this investment, Samsung Electro-Mechanics plans to actively respond to the
    growing demand for high-value-added semiconductor substrates in high-growth markets
    such as AI servers, HPC, and automotive electronics. In particular, this investment is being
    pursued based on medium- to long-term cooperation with global big tech and
    semiconductor customers. The investment includes customer funding support and
    medium- to long-term volume guarantees; thus, the company expects to strengthen the
    competitiveness of its FCBGA business based on a stable demand foundation.

    LG Innotek (011070.KS, covered by Ryan Kim)

                          (MOU) with Haiphong, Vietnam, for an investment to expand its semiconductor substrate
                          plant. Under the agreement, LG Innotek will push to build a semiconductor substrate

                              • Construction will begin in July 2026 and is scheduled to be completed in May
                                 2027.
                              • The site spans approximately 330,000 square meters (98,000 pyeong), equivalent
                                 to 45 soccer fields.
                              • According to a news report, LG Innotek will invest approximately $1 billion, or
                                 about 1.53 trillion won, for its Phase 1 expansion plan, which mainly includes RF-SiP
                                 (radio frequency system-in-package) and FC-CSP (flip chip-chip scale package).
                              • ABF substrates will be part of the Phase 2 expansion plan, but no details or
                                 investment size has been disclosed, yet.


                          According to a press release from LG Innotek on September 30, LG Innotek started mass
                          production of ABF substrates for PC chipsets targeting big tech clients last year. It
                          initiated high-volume mass production of FC-BGA for PC CPUs in the third quarter of this
                          year. Simultaneously, the company is rapidly boosting revenue by securing additional
                          major clients. Starting next year, it plans to sequentially enter the AI accelerator and AI
                          server markets.

                              • Revenue from LG Innotek's package solution business has maintained an upward
                                 trajectory for three consecutive years. With the package solution business
                                 demonstrating tangible results alongside its optical solution business, the
                                 company has strengthened its capacity to generate stable earnings.
                              • LG Innotek plans to rapidly expand its market share in the emerging semiconductor
                                 substrate market, aiming to build its package solution business, including
                                 semiconductor substrates, into a business generating US$743 million in operating
                                 profit by 2031.
                              • In the future, LG Innotek plans to develop its future businesses, including
                                 semiconductor substrates and physical AI solutions, to US$5.94 billion by 2030.
                                 The company aims to have such future new businesses account for 25% of total
                                 revenue, thereby completing a well-balanced business portfolio.


                          The expanded plant will produce major semiconductor substrates including radio
                          frequency system-in-package (RF-SiP), flip chip chip scale package (FC-CSP), and flip chip
                          ball grid array (FC-BGA). "The Gumi site will serve as a 'mother factory' responsible for
                          developing new semiconductor substrate technologies and producing new models and
                          high-value-added products, while the expanded plant in Vietnam will be operated as a
                          production base for general-purpose semiconductor substrates," an LG Innotek official
                          explained.

                          AT&S (ATSV.VI, Not Covered)

                          On June 15, AT&S announced that it had signed key terms with AMD and Marvell to add
                          AI/HPC IC substrate capacity in Kulim, Malaysia. The company said the €1.5-2bn
                          investment (approximately US$1.68bn to US$2.24bn) is fully supported and financed by
                          long-term customer commitments, pending final execution.

    Shinko (private)

    On September 30, Shinko announced that it has entered into a purchase agreement with
    Japan Display Inc. (JDI) to acquire its Mobara fab. In addition, it has entered into a sale
    agreement with FICT Ltd. for the transfer of a portion of the fab to be acquired.

         • Shinko will position the fab as a new core plant for advanced semiconductor
           packages, and strengthen its production systems for flip-chip type packages
           through the determination and implementation of capital investment plans for the
           fab in conjunction with capacity expansion at its plants in the Nagano area.
           Through these initiatives, Shinko aims to respond accurately to strong market
           demand while pursuing sustainable business growth and enhancing corporate
           value.
         • The JDI Mobara fab has a total land area of 373,483 square meters, with Shinko
           using the eastern area of the Fab (140,738 square meters, or ~38%) and FICT
           planning to use the western area (232,745 square meters, or ~62%).


    Toppan (7911.T, Not Covered)

    According to news, Toppan broke ground in March 2024 on a new factory on Pesawat
    Drive near Singapore's Jurong Lake District, built through its local unit Advanced Substrate
    Technologies (AST), a JV with Broadcom. It makes FC-BGA substrates, which is Toppan's
    term for them. It is Toppan's first FC-BGA plant outside Japan. The plant opening
    ceremony took place on September 30, 2026.

         • AST operates a facility of approximately 70,000 m² in the vicinity of Jurong Lake
           District and employs more than 200 highly skilled engineers and technicians.
         • Focus on high-demand, large-size, high-layer-count substrates
         • While the investment size is not disclosed directly by the company, Nikkei sized
           the investment at around ¥50 billion (~US$317mn).


    Daeduck (353200.KS, Not Covered)

    Daeduck announced on July 20, 2026, that it is investing ₩497 billion (~US$370M)
    manufacturing facilities and related infrastructure for semiconductor products, running
    through December 31, 2027.

    ABF capex is stepping up, but announced investment still falls short of implied
    demand. We estimate that ABF substrate makers have announced ~US$14.3bn of
    investment year to date, materially above the segment’s aggregate annual capex in recent
    years, although these commitments span multiple years. Our tally is not exhaustive. LG
    Innotek has yet to disclose the size of its planned ABF capacity investment, while Shinko
    has not quantified the additional spending required to expand capacity following its
    announced acquisition of a JDI fab.

    Our supply chain checks suggest that each US$1 of investment can support US$0.50–
    0.60 of annual revenue at full ramp. On this basis, the US$14.3bn announced so far could
    support US$7.2–8.6bn of incremental annual revenue. This compares with US$11.4bn of
    incremental revenue implied by our industry forecast. We model the ABF substrate
    market reaching US$20.9bn in 2030, up from US$9.5bn in 2026. Despite the step-up in

The State of the Current Cycle

                             The ABF substrate market has gone through a few cycles over the past two
                             decades. We believe we are now still in the early innings of an up-cycle.


                          There was a prolonged down-cycle from 2012-18 as the PC TAM shrank amid the rise of
                          smartphones and tablets. During this tough period, companies were not able to generate
                          profits and had to compete on price to fill their idle capacity. As a result, during those
                          years, there was no or very limited capacity expansion, and capital expenditures by the
                          major ABF substrate suppliers were kept at a minimum.

                          Even as general server demand picked up, lifting utilization rates across the group going
                          into 2020, ABF substrate suppliers remained cautious on the longer-term demand outlook
                          and remained disciplined, hesitating to expand capacity. Hence, capex turned up just
                          slightly in 2019-20, increasing ~US$600mn vs. ~US$2.2bn on average per year in 2012-18.

                          This underinvestment led to sudden undersupply, as the shock from Covid-19 drove strong
                          work-from-home demand for PCs, as well as increased data usage and storage for general
                          computing driven by online entertainment. This ultimately led to a significant increase in
                          ABF substrate market value from 2020-22, reflected by the sudden surge in demand
                          along with meaningful pricing adjustments owing to the lack of supply.

                          During this 2020-22 period, much capacity expansion was set in motion as ABF substrate
                          suppliers and customers came to agree that necessary investments were needed for
                          future growth. Some subsidies were even given to these suppliers to facilitate this
                          capacity expansion. This is why capex jumped from ~US$2.9bn in 2020 to US$4.1bn in
                          2021 and US$5.5bn in 2022; even in 2023-24, capex remained elevated, as capacity
                          expansion plans continued.

                          Unfortunately, demand did not play out as expected. As the world came out of the
                          pandemic, demand for PCs and online entertainment fell sharply. This normalization of
                          demand, coupled with capacity expansion from practically every major ABF substrate
                          supplier, resulted in the ABF substrate market once again becoming oversupplied. This led
                          to a sharp decline in ABF substrate market value in 2023-24, as volumes normalized,
                          driving prices down to normalize against the new supply/demand dynamic.

                          Fortunately, cloud demand remained strong for general computing, and with AI demand
                          starting to pick up, the down-cycle this time around was much shorter (two years) vs. the
                          prior down-cycle (six years).

                          In 1H24, the ABF substrate market troughed and we saw an upward inflection since then,
                          but the pace of the recovery has been moderate and bifurcated. Midrange/low-end
                          markets such as PCs have shown moderate demand recovery, with high-end server and AI-
                          related end-demand recovering and growing at a faster pace. This is why we turned the
                          page on our bearish stance in 1H25, but did not turn more bullish until early 2026.

                                                                   Breaking down ABF substrate end demand

                                                                   The end market mix for ABF substrates has shifted dramatically over the past decade. PCs
                                                                   were once the dominant demand driver, accounting for approximately 70% of global ABF
                                                                   substrate market value in 2015, supported primarily by PC CPUs and GPUs. Since then,
                                                                   however, the industry's demand profile has undergone a structural transformation. We
                                                                   estimate that PC-related applications represented only ~23% of total ABF substrate
                                                                   market value in 2025, and this share is expected to decline further to below 10% by 2030.

                                                                   In contrast, demand from servers, AI GPUs, AI ASICs, and networking applications has
                                                                   expanded rapidly. We estimate that these segments collectively accounted for only
                                                                   around 10% of the ABF substrate market in 2015, but their share increased to ~60% by
                                                                   2025. Looking ahead, we expect they will represent more than 80% of total ABF
                                                                   substrate market value by 2030.

                                                                   In our view, this structural shift in end-market demand has been the primary driver of ABF
                                                                   substrate industry growth over the past decade and will become even more pronounced
                                                                   over the next five years. As AI infrastructure deployment accelerates, we expect continued
                                                                   expansion in server, AI accelerator, and networking demand to drive meaningful
                                                                   acceleration in ABF substrate market growth.

Price Target and Valuation Methodology
                   Our 12-month price target increases ~21% to NT$1,775 (from NT$1,465), driven by our
                   increased earnings estimates for CY26-28: We believe the company's earnings have
                   returned to a growth track from 2026 onward and will show stronger growth in 2027,
                   driven by the high-end ABF substrate market's reversion to undersupply and Unimicron's
                   dominant supply share in AI ASICs and also server CPUs, which puts it in a favorable
                   position to benefit from rising AI investments.

                   We believe the overall ABF substrate market bottomed in 2H24, and see growth
                   accelerating from 2H26 onward with the ramp of multiple next-generation, large body size
                   ABF substrates for new server GPUs, CPUs, ASICs, and networking chips. New
                   technologies such as embedded passives and Intel's EMIB-T should also increase the
                   manufacturing complexity of the package substrates, which adds to the under-capacity as
                   usable output decreases.

                   Similar to our analysis of other tech hardware companies within our coverage, we use a
                   residual income (RI) valuation model to value Unimicron – we think it derives the most
                   accurate value of the firm as it takes into account cost of equity. Our key assumptions

                                      ° Equity risk premium of 8.7%;
                               ° Beta of 1.0;
                            • Medium-term growth rate of 14% (slightly lowered from 15%)
                            • Terminal growth rate of 3% (unchanged, similar to the rest of the companies under

Price Target and Valuation Methodology
                          Our price target increases ~29%, to NT$2,000, reflecting our raised earnings
                          estimates for CY26-28: We believe the company's earnings have returned to a growth
                          track from 2026 onward and will show stronger growth in 2027, driven by the high-end
                          ABF substrate market's reversion to undersupply, NYPCB's dominant supply share for
                          networking chips, and its proactive pricing strategy, which puts it in a favorable position to
                          benefit from rising AI investments.

                          We believe the overall ABF substrate market bottomed in 2H24, and growth should
                          accelerate from 2H26 onward with the ramp of multiple next-generation, large body size
                          ABF substrates for new server GPUs, CPUs, ASICs and networking chips. New
                          technologies, such as embedded passives and Intel's EMIB-T, should also increase
                          manufacturing complexity of the package substrates, adding to the overall undercapacity
                          as usable output decreases.

                          Similar to our analysis of other tech hardware companies within our coverage, we use a
                          residual income (RI) valuation model to value NYPCB – we think it derives the most
                          accurate value of the firm given that it takes into account cost of equity. Key assumptions
                          (all unchanged):

                                   • Cost of equity of 9.3%;
                                              ° Risk-free rate of 1% (10-year Taiwan government note yield);
                                              ° Equity risk premium of 8.7%;
                                      ° Beta of 1.0;
                                   • Medium-term growth rate of 17% – fair given our analysis of the substrate market
                                         over the next couple of years;
                                   • Terminal growth rate of 3% (similar to the rest of the companies under our tech
                                         hardware coverage).


                          Our bull and bear case values increase by similar magnitudes, to NT$3,575 and NT
                          $1,020, respectively.

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Supply/Demand Update: Undersupply Deepens in CY27–28
                  Our updated model points to a wider supply shortfall in CY27–28, despite additional
                  capacity: Incorporating the latest expansion plans and semiconductor demand forecasts,
                  we now expect ABF substrate demand to exceed available supply by 9.3% in CY27 and
                  13.7% in CY28, versus 6.2% and 9.4% previously. This represents a widening of 3.1ppt and
                  4.3ppt, respectively, relative to our prior estimates. We maintain our view that CY26 is a
                  broadly balanced market, followed by increasingly tight supply over the next two years.

                  The main demand upgrade comes from other ASICs, including Chinese AI chips: We
                  raise our shipment assumptions for this category to 6.4mn units in CY27 and 8.7mn in
                  CY28, from 4.6mn and 6.2mn previously. Our Nvidia GPU and server CPU forecasts remain
                  largely unchanged, while we lower AMD GPU estimates while also keeping CY27 Trainium
                  and TPU shipments largely unchanged. The tighter substrate outlook therefore reflects
                  stronger demand across a broader set of ASIC suppliers, rather than higher shipment
                  assumptions for every major AI platform. We also raise our substrate content assumptions
                  for select chips based on our latest supply chain checks, lifting our substrate demand
                  estimates across some segments, including server CPUs and networking.

                  Higher supply assumptions provide limited relief in CY27-28: We now include additional
                  capacity announcements that have been announced recently, including two additional
                  Kinsus factories, scheduled to come online in CY28 and CY29, beyond the CY27 expansion
                  already in our model. Several larger projects, however, contribute later. NYPCB’s new site
                  starts ramping in 2H29, while SEMCO’s Sejong expansion begins mass production in
                  September 2028 and its project in Vietnam is scheduled to begin operations by June
                  2030. These additions increase medium-term supply but do not prevent the modeled
                  shortfall from worsening through CY28.

                  Increasing substrate complexity adds to the pressure on usable output: Larger body
                  sizes, higher layer counts, and more demanding manufacturing processes constrain the
                  output available to meet demand, even as suppliers expand installed capacity. With the
                  supply gap widening in CY27-28, we expect tightness to become a more important pricing
                  driver than raw material cost pass-through. This supports our forecast for 25%+ price
                  increases in CY27 and further increases in CY28, alongside continued margin expansion.

    NYPCB (8046.TW, OW, covered by Howard Kao)

    On August 6, NYPCB announced that its Board of Directors had approved a capex budget
    of NT$46.8bn (~US$1,474mn) to invest in building a new ABF substrate production site.
    Our checks indicate that this production site is located in the southern part of Taiwan, and
    will start to ramp up production in 2H29. Given the size of this investment, we estimate
    that it will approximately double its capacity exiting CY30, relative to its CY28 capacity.

    Kinsus (3189.TW, Not Covered)

    In our previous model, we had assumed only one factory (k6b) coming online in CY27,
    increasing capacity ~30%. However, recent checks suggest that Kinsus intends to bring
    two more factories online, one in CY28 (k6c) and one in CY29 (k6d). This implies that
    capacity would increase another ~25% in CY28 and ~20% in CY29, bringing Kinsus' total
    ABF substrate capacity to almost double exiting CY29, relative to its CY26 capacity.

    Ibiden (4062.T, covered by Shoji Sato)

    Back in February, Ibiden first announced that it will invest capex of ¥500bn in the
    electronics field planned through F3/29, for ABF substrate expansion. Sato-san's latest
    view is that Ibiden will need a new factory building to install the equipment and facilities
    that will be purchased with the ¥500bn. As a result, Sato-san expects Ibiden during its 2Q
    results briefing (October 30) to announce plans to make a large capital investment,
    including for a factory building with a long lead time, and raise its medium-term earnings
    forecast (report here).

    SEMCO (009150.KS, covered by Shawn Kim)

    On September 29, SEMCO announced investment of KRW4.27 trillion (~US$3,178mn) in
    Sejong and KRW2.51 trillion (~US$1,488mn) in Vietnam, for AI server semiconductor
    substrate capacity expansion.

        • Sejong: Investment period from September 2026 to May 2028, with mass
           production starting in September 2028. Largest single-product investment to date,
           serving as key hub for mass production of high-value-added, highly demanding
           products, proactively responding to the increasing demand for AI server substrates.
        • Vietnam: The Vietnamese subsidiary aims to complete construction and begin
           operations by June 2030. It will be operated as a strategic hub to respond to global
           volume demand and enhance production efficiency through a stable supply
           system.


    With this investment, Samsung Electro-Mechanics plans to actively respond to the
    growing demand for high-value-added semiconductor substrates in high-growth markets
    such as AI servers, HPC, and automotive electronics. In particular, this investment is being
    pursued based on medium- to long-term cooperation with global big tech and
    semiconductor customers. The investment includes customer funding support and
    medium- to long-term volume guarantees; thus, the company expects to strengthen the
    competitiveness of its FCBGA business based on a stable demand foundation.

The State of the Current Cycle

                             The ABF substrate market has gone through a few cycles over the past two
                             decades. We believe we are now still in the early innings of an up-cycle.


                          There was a prolonged down-cycle from 2012-18 as the PC TAM shrank amid the rise of
                          smartphones and tablets. During this tough period, companies were not able to generate
                          profits and had to compete on price to fill their idle capacity. As a result, during those
                          years, there was no or very limited capacity expansion, and capital expenditures by the
                          major ABF substrate suppliers were kept at a minimum.

                          Even as general server demand picked up, lifting utilization rates across the group going
                          into 2020, ABF substrate suppliers remained cautious on the longer-term demand outlook
                          and remained disciplined, hesitating to expand capacity. Hence, capex turned up just
                          slightly in 2019-20, increasing ~US$600mn vs. ~US$2.2bn on average per year in 2012-18.

                          This underinvestment led to sudden undersupply, as the shock from Covid-19 drove strong
                          work-from-home demand for PCs, as well as increased data usage and storage for general
                          computing driven by online entertainment. This ultimately led to a significant increase in
                          ABF substrate market value from 2020-22, reflected by the sudden surge in demand
                          along with meaningful pricing adjustments owing to the lack of supply.

                          During this 2020-22 period, much capacity expansion was set in motion as ABF substrate
                          suppliers and customers came to agree that necessary investments were needed for
                          future growth. Some subsidies were even given to these suppliers to facilitate this
                          capacity expansion. This is why capex jumped from ~US$2.9bn in 2020 to US$4.1bn in
                          2021 and US$5.5bn in 2022; even in 2023-24, capex remained elevated, as capacity
                          expansion plans continued.

                          Unfortunately, demand did not play out as expected. As the world came out of the
                          pandemic, demand for PCs and online entertainment fell sharply. This normalization of
                          demand, coupled with capacity expansion from practically every major ABF substrate
                          supplier, resulted in the ABF substrate market once again becoming oversupplied. This led
                          to a sharp decline in ABF substrate market value in 2023-24, as volumes normalized,
                          driving prices down to normalize against the new supply/demand dynamic.

                          Fortunately, cloud demand remained strong for general computing, and with AI demand
                          starting to pick up, the down-cycle this time around was much shorter (two years) vs. the
                          prior down-cycle (six years).

                          In 1H24, the ABF substrate market troughed and we saw an upward inflection since then,
                          but the pace of the recovery has been moderate and bifurcated. Midrange/low-end
                          markets such as PCs have shown moderate demand recovery, with high-end server and AI-
                          related end-demand recovering and growing at a faster pace. This is why we turned the
                          page on our bearish stance in 1H25, but did not turn more bullish until early 2026.

                                                                   Breaking down ABF substrate end demand

                                                                   The end market mix for ABF substrates has shifted dramatically over the past decade. PCs
                                                                   were once the dominant demand driver, accounting for approximately 70% of global ABF
                                                                   substrate market value in 2015, supported primarily by PC CPUs and GPUs. Since then,
                                                                   however, the industry's demand profile has undergone a structural transformation. We
                                                                   estimate that PC-related applications represented only ~23% of total ABF substrate
                                                                   market value in 2025, and this share is expected to decline further to below 10% by 2030.

                                                                   In contrast, demand from servers, AI GPUs, AI ASICs, and networking applications has
                                                                   expanded rapidly. We estimate that these segments collectively accounted for only
                                                                   around 10% of the ABF substrate market in 2015, but their share increased to ~60% by
                                                                   2025. Looking ahead, we expect they will represent more than 80% of total ABF
                                                                   substrate market value by 2030.

                                                                   In our view, this structural shift in end-market demand has been the primary driver of ABF
                                                                   substrate industry growth over the past decade and will become even more pronounced
                                                                   over the next five years. As AI infrastructure deployment accelerates, we expect continued
                                                                   expansion in server, AI accelerator, and networking demand to drive meaningful
                                                                   acceleration in ABF substrate market growth.

產業報告                                                                                  台灣


                        半導體產業
                     封測產業：資本支出與擴產規模創歷史新高
                     重要訊息
 焦點內容                台灣封測廠 2026-27 年資本支出與擴產規模將創歷史新高。
                     評論及分析
                     數十年難得一見的成長機會。台灣前八大封測廠年初迄今已上修 2026 年資本
 1. 數十年難得一見的成長機會。    支出 45.9%至 4,839 億元，創歷史新高，較 2025 年幾乎翻倍(年增 99%，相
 2. 先進封裝與晶圓測試需求龐大。   較過去 10 年複合年成長率 15.4%)。我們認為大幅擴產主要反映：(1) AI 晶
 3. 大規模擴產將加重財務負擔。    片出貨強勁帶動既有業務成長；(2)晶片尺寸擴大及設計複雜度提高，將消耗
                     更多產能；(3)台積電(2330 TT，NT$2,490，增加持股)將資源重新配置至先進
                     製程與先進封裝，並逐步退出晶圓測試(CP)等毛利率較低或非核心業務。由
                     於上述成長動能均屬結構性因素，我們預期封測廠未來兩年資本支出仍將維
                     持高檔。
                     先進封裝與晶圓測試需求龐大。目前我們擁有的資訊仍不足以精確估算 AI 晶
                     片 CP 測試市場規模。然而，根據我們的初步估算及供應鏈調查，AI 晶片 CP
                     測試營收規模預估達 500-600 億元，且將隨測試時間增加而持續成長。在假
                     設每投入 1 元資本支出可創造 0.5 元營收的情境下，我們預估 CP 測試所需資
                     本支出將超過 1,000 億元，占 2026 年封測廠整體資本支出 20-25%。我們預
                     估台灣封測廠資本密集度將由 2025 年的 28.9%升至 2026 年的 44.1% (過去
                     10 年平均為 16.6%)，部分公司甚至超過 100%，遠高於半導體產業平均的
                     15.5% (記憶體產業 2026 年營收預期成長超過 280%，拉低整體產業平均資
                     本密集度)。
                     大規模擴產將加重財務負擔。在封測廠中，以測試業務為主的公司因資本密
                     集度較高，故面臨的財務壓力可能更大，包括京元電子(2449 TT，NT$296.5，
                     增加持股；資本密集度 104%)、欣銓(3264 TT，NT$278，未評等；62%)及
                     台星科(3265 TT，NT$292.5，未評等；235%；其雖以封裝業務為主，但新
                     增產能主要用於 CP 測試)。而日月光投控(3711 TT，NT$747，增加持股)整體
                     資本密集度相對同業較低，但若僅考量 AI 業務營收及相關擴產，資本密集度
                     亦超過 100%。我們認為封測廠資本支出仍具進一步上修空間，因此多數業
                     者 2026-27 年將面臨龐大的資金需求。例如，京元電子近期宣布與 NVIDIA (美)
                     簽訂客戶預付款協議，以支應美國產能擴充。NVIDIA 亦與 Amkor (美)簽訂價
                     值 15 億美元的協議，透過預付款及多年期策略生產合作支持其擴產。我們預
                     期後續將有更多封測廠會透過海外可轉債、聯貸、現金增資及可轉債來進行
                     籌資，預估 2027 年封測廠折舊費用將年增 30-100%。
                     投資建議
                     我們預期封測廠積極擴大資本支出與產能將有利於：(1)設備供應商，包括
                     Advantest( 日 ) 、 鴻 勁 (7769 TT， NT$5,780 ， 增 加 持 股 ) 及 致 茂 (2360 TT，
                     NT$2,250，未評等)；(2)測試介面供應商，包括中華精測(6510 TT，NT$3,225,
凱基投顧
                     增加持股)、穎崴(6515 TT，NT$5,615，增加持股)及旺矽(6223 TT，NT$5,885，
潘俊宏                  增加持股)。封測族群中，我們看好 CPU 業務占比較高的日月光投控，係因

       伺服器業務優於預期，4Q26 營運續強 : 3Q26 營收 45.02 億元，季增 20.4%、年
       增 26.2%，較我們原先預估低約 8%，主要受到手機客戶拉貨動能不如預期影響。
       惟 GB300 與 VR200 QD 持續出貨，帶動伺服器業務維持強勁成長，預期伺服器
       相關營收占比將由 2Q26 的 56%提升至 80～85%，有助於優化產品組合並提升
       獲利能力。因此我們上調 3Q26 毛利率預估至 37.05%，EPS 亦調升至 16.97 元 。

       展望 4Q26，隨 VR200 出貨量進一步增加、多項 ASIC 平台 QD 逐步放量，我們
       預期營收將季增 18.7%至 53.44 億元；受惠伺服器產品占比提升及生產效率改
       善，毛利率可望再季增約 0.3 個百分點至 37.35%，EPS 預估為 20.22 元，營收
       與獲利均有望續創成長。

       雙 面 水 冷 板 推 動 接 頭 設 計 變 革 ， 富 世 達 單 機 價 值 量 可 望 再 提 升 :目 前 AMD 與
       AWS 已採用雙面水冷板設計，根據供應鏈調查， Google TPU V9 及 NVIDIA
       VRU 亦有望跟進。隨著垂直供電(VPD)設計導入，伺服器內部可供水路配置的
       空 間受 到壓縮 ，帶 動雙面 水冷 板及微 型快 速接頭 (MQD/Mini QD)的 應用 需求 。
       另一方面，為滿足更高冷卻液流量需求，部分接頭亦有望由 UQD 升級至單價較
       高的 ZQD。上述設計變化若逐步落地，將分別透過接頭用量增加、微型接頭導
       入及高單價產品升級，創造單機 QD 價值量的額外成長空間，進一步挹注富世
       達 2027 年營收與獲利表現。

  代理 AI 讓 CPU 工作量增加：從回覆問題，走向執行任務

 案傳回給用戶。主節點CPU負責調度、I/O和系統管理，而GPU則負責繁重的運
 算任務。
現在：代理AI不再只是回答一個問題，而是將目標分解成多個步驟，決定下一步
 該做什麼，調用多個模型，查詢資料庫，連接API，運行企業應用程序，檢查權
 限，檢索內存，驗證輸出，然後再次循環執行整個過程。                     僅
CPU負責：編排：管理分解複雜任務的引擎。代理執行和工具呼叫：觸發 API 和 供
 傳統企業軟體。策略與安全：對每個自主操作進行實際檢查。
隨 AI 從模型推論延伸至 Agent 執行，CPU 的角色擴及任務協調、工具操作及資 參
 料處理。AMD 5 月官方文章已描述 CPU：GPU 由過去約 1：4–8，朝 1：1 移 考
 動；Intel Q2 法說進一步表示，目前以顆數計已接近均衡。兩家原廠的觀察，支

Equity Research
Sector Report | Semiconductor｜Oct 13, 2026


                                                                                                     Overseas
                                                                                                     Technology
ASIC Update TPU v9 Timeline, v10 Opportunities

  Jeff Pu, CFA                         Henry Huang
  SFC CE No. BNO719                    SFC CE No. BYA749
  jeffpu@gfgroup.com.hk                henryhuang@gfgroup.com.hk


What’s New?

Following the recent speculations of TPU v9 delay, we provide our view on the updated TPU v9 timeline and volume. We expect near-
term headwinds for MTK. For mid to long term, we continue to like MRVL and MTK.

Comments

We push out our TPU v9 Humufish expectations by one quarter: Following our U.S. marketing trip in the 2nd week of October, we
sensed that a delay in Humufish is somewhat anticipated by U.S. investors. Based on our supply chain research, we believe Humufish’s
Core A design, by Google, schedule has slipped by ~3 weeks, likely due to a redesign, which in turn requires modifications to MTK’s Core
B and I/O. While the sampling target remains November, we now expect the tape-out to slip to January 2027, with the mass-production
tape-out pushed to 2Q27 and shipments likely delayed to 1Q28. Nevertheless, as highlighted in our September 30 report of MTK: 100%
EMIB-T Market Share in TPU v9, we remain constructive on EMIB-T’s substrate yield improvements. We believe the supply chain has
identified the root causes of the EMIB substrate yield, potentially paving the way for a yield re-acceleration from current 45-50%.

Google's TPU undersupply to its own AI models: Despite accelerating demand for Google's TPUs, there was competition for compute
resources between Google and external customers, particularly Anthropic. The recently unveiled Gemini 4, likely pre-trained on ~200k
TPU v7 clusters, delivers strong performance in coding, reasoning, enterprise applications, cybersecurity, and the catch-up in recursive
self-improvement (RSI). However, Google appears to have lagged, as a substantial portion of its TPU v7 was allocated to external
customers, particularly in 1H26. Although Google is increasing internal TPU allocations in 2H26, competition for compute resources
remains intense, yet, the increasing TPU v7 allocation to in-house could lead to a better set-up for its next-generation Gemini models.
According to SemiAnalysis, it highlighted the widening compute gap between Google DeepMind and leading AI labs, with Anthropic and
OpenAI potentially adding 5–10GW of capacity each in 2027, compared with only a few GW for Google.

Google TPU demand, v10 dynamics and EMIB-T: We maintain our Broadcom Sunfish forecasts outlined in our June 16 report of June
Edition, including 460k CoWoS wafers for ASICs in 2027, with Sunfish shipments still expected to begin in late 2026. Meanwhile, we
expect MTK’s Zebrafish shipments to extend into 2027–28 at higher volumes, partially offsetting TPU v9 schedule risks. For TPU v10
(4Q28/1Q29), we continue to view Icefish, supplied by MTK and GUC (3DIC), as the only confirmed mainstream SKU based on A14, while
Merope remains uncertain, with Broadcom potentially facing competition from AMD (compute) and Marvell (I/O). Following v9’s 100%
adoption of EMIB-T, we see growing momentum for EMIB-T in v10. In addition to Icefish’s likely adoption, Merope is also being evaluated
for EMIB-T packaging due to its large-reticle design.

Comments

We expect near-term headwinds for MTK, yet for mid-to-long term, we still like MRVL (ASIC of $17bn in FY29E, AI networking, DSP),
MTK (intact v8t, 100% share in v9, potential 2nd/3rd datacenter customers!), and Intel (EMIB-T) in Google’s ASIC supply chain.

Risks:

1) AI demand slowdown, 2) infrastructure deployment, 3) supply constraints, 4) competition.

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial

                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

                                              departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not
                                              factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

Executive Summary
                    Higher optical engine shipment assumptions as yields
                    improve

                    Our semi team has lifted their optical engine shipment assumptions following their latest
                    supply-chain checks. While PIC production remains a bottleneck, improving SoIC yields
                    and downstream assembly yields should support a faster OE ramp. They now expect OE
                    production to reach 2mn/59mn/148mn units in 2026/27/28, with actual OE shipments
                    reaching 0.39mn/17.73mn/73.87mn units, respectively. In particular, they assume the SoIC
                    yield improves from 50% in 2026 to 95% in 2027 onwards, while downstream assembly
                    yield rises from 20% in 2026 to 30%/50% in 2027/28. We believe this provides greater
                    confidence in the CPO volume ramp, although downstream assembly and testing remain
                    key gating factors for how quickly OE shipments can scale.

                        Voltronic Power (6409.TW)
                        Recharging Growth: UPS Recovery and HVDC Potential; Initiate at Buy
                        CITI'S TAKE

                        We initiate coverage on Voltronic with a Buy rating and NT$1,050 target
                        price. Voltronic is a Taiwan-based UPS ODM, supplying to western power
                                                                                                                 n
                        vendors including Schneider, Riello, Vertiv and Eaton. We view 2026E as the              Buy
                        earnings trough, with improving online UPS mix and operating leverage                    Price (13 Oct 26 13:30)      NT$854.00
                        driving 28% earnings rebound in 2027E. Structural outsourcing by western
                        power vendors should support sustained share gains, while expansion into                 Target price                NT$1,050.00
                        HVDC power racks offers a new stream for AIDC growth, supporting a                       Expected share price return       23.0%
                        potential re-rating. Our TP applies 25x 2027E EPS against earnings CAGR                  Expected dividend yield            3.5%
                        of 20% in 2026-2028E, broadly consistent with its L-T historical average.
                                                                                                                 Expected total return             26.5%
                        Outsourcing and mix upgrade underpin the recovery — Western vendors’                     Market Cap                  NT$75,369M
                        increasing focus on integrated AIDC infrastructure strengthens the rationale for                                      US$2,359M
                        outsourcing select UPS platforms. Voltronic’s customization capabilities and
                        flexible manufacturing position it to capture additional opportunities. A rising
                        contribution from online and higher power UPS should support margins, driving EPS
                        CAGR of 20% in 2026-2028E.                                                               Price Performance
                        Power racks could materially broaden its growth opportunity — Voltronic’s high           (RIC: 6409.TW, BB: 6409 TT)
                        voltage EV-charger experience and longstanding relationships with western power
                        vendors support its entry into HVDC power solutions. It has progressed into
                        customer sampling, with management indicating that HVDC power rack mass
                        production could begin in 2H27E at the earliest. Successful commercialization could
                        broaden its addressable market and support a valuation re-rating.

                        Earnings recovery and strong cash returns — We view 2026E as the earnings
                        trough, followed by a recovery in 2027-2028E. A richer online UPS mix and operating
                        leverage should lift GPM from 27.1% in 2026E to 28.1% and 29.0% in 2027E and
                        2028E, respectively. Its relatively asset-light business model, net cash position and
                        high dividend payout should provide additional support for shareholder returns.

                        Initiate Buy with TP NT$1,050 on 25x 2027E EPS — Our target multiple is broadly
                        consistent with Voltronic’s average forward P/E since 2013, supported by its
                        competitive position in UPS outsourcing and durable customer relationships.
                        Clearer evidence of power-rack commercialization could offer further re-rating.

                                                    Executive Summary
                                                    We initiate coverage of Voltronic with a Buy rating and target price of NT$1,050
                                                    (25x 2027E EPS), supported by structural UPS outsourcing, improving product mix
                                                    and emerging opportunities in AI datacenter power infrastructure. Voltronic is a
                                                    Taiwan-based ODM of uninterrupted power supplies (“UPS”) and power
                                                    conversion products for global brands. UPS system provides backup electricity and
                                                    protection against power disturbances, helping critical equipment maintain
                                                    operation during supply disruptions. UPS accounted for 63% of Voltronic’s 2025
                                                    group sales. Its pure-play ODM model, customization capabilities and
                                                    longstanding customer relationships underpin its competitive positioning.

                                                    Our positive stance on the shares is based on three major reasons:

                                                    1.   We see expansion into HVDC power racks as a potentially significant new
                                                         growth opportunity. Its experience in high-voltage EV chargers provides
                                                         relevant engineering capabilities, while its established relationships with
                                                         western power vendors support access to customer development programs.
                                                         Voltronic has progressed into customer sampling, with management
                                                         indicating that HVDC power rack mass production could begin in 2H27E at the
                                                         earliest. Successful commercialization could broaden its addressable market
                                                         and support a valuation re-rating, although meaningful earnings contribution
                                                         remains subject to qualification, design wins and production schedules.

                                                    2.   Structural UPS outsourcing should support sustained market share gains.
                                                         Western power vendors are allocating more resources to integrated AIDC
                                                         infrastructure and energy management, strengthening the rationale for
                                                         outsourcing selected products. Voltronic’s engineering expertise, flexible
                                                         manufacturing and ability to handle a broad range of customized products in
                                                         small batches make it well positioned to capture these opportunities.

                                                    3.   The shift toward online and higher power UPS should improve revenue quality
                                                         and profitability. We expect online UPS to be the principal driver of the
                                                         earnings recovery, with online UPS sales growing 12% CAGR in 2026-2028E as
                                                         outsourcing opportunities and demand for higher power systems expand.

                                                    We view 2026E as the earnings trough, followed by a recovery in 2027-2028E. We
                                                    forecast EPS of NT$33.00/NT$42.30/NT$47.25 in 2026E/2027E/2028E, implying
                                                    earnings growth of 28% and 12% in 2027E and 2028E. A richer online UPS mix and
                                                    operating leverage should lift GPM from 27.1% in 2026E to 28.1% and 29.0% in
                                                    2027E and 2028E, respectively. Its relatively asset-light business model, net cash
                                                    position and high dividend payout should provide additional support for
                                                    shareholder returns.

                                                    Voltronic’s long tern average forward P/E since 2013. We believe its competitive
                                                    position in UPS outsourcing, durable customer relationships and manufacturing
                                                    capabilities justify this multiple, with clearer evidence of power rack
                                                    commercialization offering potential for further re-rating.

                                                    Investment Thesis
                                                    Positive #1 – AIDC creates a new growth runway, with
                                                    power-rack expansion potentially lifting Voltronic into
                                                    broader power solutions
                                                    We see Voltronic’s expansion into power racks as a potentially significant extension
                                                    of its AIDC opportunity in the medium to long term, enabling the company to
                                                    capture the broader share of datacenter power spending. We believe Voltronic’s
                                                    existing high-voltage engineering capabilities, established relationships with
                                                    western power vendors and customer collaboration provide a credible foundation
                                                    for winning business in HVDC power rack.

                                                    Rapid growth in AI workloads and rising rack density increase the power capacity
                                                    required, alongside more demanding requirements for efficiency, reliability and
                                                    load management. Nvidia’s roadmap targets 800VDC infrastructure supporting
                                                    racks of 1MW and beyond, while its latest architecture includes power racks that
                                                    supply 800VDC to compute racks within existing AC-powered facilities. We believe
                                                    this creates scope for greater power-infrastructure, even as the architecture
                                                    consolidates conversion stages to improve efficiency.

                                                    EV-charger experience provides a relevant technical foundation for HVDC
                                                    development

                                                    Voltronic already offers DC fast chargers ranging 30-240kW, with modular designs
                                                    delivering constant power across a 300-100VDC range and charging controls
                                                    developed internally. These products demonstrate existing experience with high-
                                                    voltage conversion, protection, thermal management and modular power-system
                                                    design. We believe these capabilities should support its development of 800VDC
                                                    PSUs and reduce the engineering learning curve.

                                                    Established westerns customer relationships strengthen its route to market

                                                    Voltronic’s UPS ODM business provides existing engineering relationships and
                                                    familiarity with customers’ quality, customization and manufacturing
                                                    requirements. Its pure ODM business model also emphasizes avoiding competition
                                                    with customers. We believe this positioning makes it a suitable partner for western
                                                    vendors who are expanding their AI infrastructure offerings. Existing relationships
                                                    should help Voltronic secure development opportunities and understand product
                                                    roadmaps early, although each new platform still requires qualification.

                                                    Voltronic has already taken concrete steps toward this opportunity. The company
                                                    has publicly introduced an HVDC PSU for power racks, while its broader
                                                    development plan extends into solutions combining battery backup unit (BBUs).

                                                                                            Datacenters provide an important source of incremental demand, while
                                                                                            commercial and industrial applications broaden the market beyond the AI

                                                                                            protect critical equipment against supply disturbance. Commercial applications –
                                                                                            including offices, retail networks and healthcare facilities – require protection for

                                                                                            critical processes where power interruptions can disrupt production.

                                                                                            from a relatively small number of large brands can open substantial manufacturing
                                                                                            opportunities.

                                                                                            Western brands’ strategic priorities support further selective outsourcing

                                                                                            Per our industry checks, major UPS brands still manufacture a substantial portion
                                                                                            of their UPS products internally, while increasingly moving toward energy
                                                                                            management and committing resources to broader AIDC infrastructure. This could
                                                                                            result in small and medium UPS products to be gradually outsourced as this
                                                                                            transition develops. We view this as a multi-year opportunity, particularly where
                                                                                            established platforms can be transferred to qualified ODMs while customers retain
                                                                                            control over product specifications, branding and distribution.

                                                                                            We identify three economic reasons for this shift –

                                                                                            1.     Outsourcing can improve manufacturing and capital efficiency: A specialist
                                                                                                   ODM can aggregate demand across customers, consolidate component

                                                                                                   base. For brands, this can reduce incremental factory investment and simplify
                                                                                                   capacity planning.

                                                                                            2.     Outsourcing can accelerate product development: access to ODMs’
                                                                                                   established platforms, component knowledge and manufacturing processes
                                                                                                   allows brands to adapt existing designs for additional markets and
                                                                                                   applications. Engineering resources can then concentrate on product

                                                    Positive #3 – Online and high-power UPS mix upgrade
                                                    should support structurally better growth
                                                    We expect Voltronic’s shift toward online and higher-power UPS to become an
                                                    increasingly important driver of revenue growth and profitability. Moving up the
                                                    product range increases power capacity and engineering content per system,
                                                    supporting higher ASPs and greater differentiation. We forecast online UPS sales to
                                                    rise at a 12% CAGR in 2026-2028E, ahead of offline UPS at 6%, with online UPS
                                                    gross profit growing faster at 16% as product mix improves.

                                                    Offline UPS remains a stable revenue base, yet offers more limited differentiation.
                                                    Offline UPS typically serves home offices, small businesses and basic power
                                                    applications. These products feature relatively simple designs and lower costs.

                                                    We view this segment as increasingly mature and commoditized, with lower
                                                    technical barriers exposing suppliers to greater pricing pressure, including
                                                    competition from Chinese manufacturers. Scale, procurement efficiency and cost
                                                    control hence are the key competitive factors, while opportunities for sustained
                                                    ASP and margin expansion are more constrained, in our view. Our model assumes
                                                    offline UPS gross margin to be at 24-26% in 2025-2028E.
Prepared for Kevin Lu


                                                    Online UPS offers greater technical differentiation and stronger margin potential.
                                                    Its double-conversion architecture continuously converts AC power into DC and
                                                    back into AC, providing stable voltage and frequency, avoiding power disturbances
                                                    and enabling zero transfer time to battery operation.

                                                    It is particularly suited to complex, power-sensitive applications such as
                                                    datacenters, industrial automation and precision control systems, where even brief
                                                    interruptions or power quality disturbances can disrupt operations. The business
                                                    also exhibits high-mix, low-volume characteristics, particularly in customized

                                                    commercial and industrial applications, where customers require different power
                                                    ratings, redundancy configuration and battery interfaces etc. Our model assumes
                                                    online UPS gross margin to be at 31-34% in 2025-2028E.

                                                    We believe this creates opportunities for an experienced ODM partner such as
                                                    Voltronic to differentiate through customization and reliable delivery, while sharing
                                                    development and procurement resources across customers and product platforms.
                                                    Together with demanding certification, customer qualification and reliability
                                                    testing, these capabilities raise entry barriers and switching costs, supporting
                                                    higher ASPs, strong customer retention and better margin potential as Voltronic
                                                    expands into higher power systems.

                                                    We project online UPS sales to increase 12% CAGR in 2026-2028E, lifting its
                                                    contribution to group sales from 37% in 2025 to c.44% in 2028E. The underlying
                                                    driver comes from a stronger outsourcing opportunity thanks to the AIDC boom.
                                                    Western vendors, including Schneider, Vertiv are expanding their focus on
                                                    integrated AIDC infrastructure, power distribution, and infrastructure
                                                    management. Meanwhile, rising power requirements within conventional AC-
                                                    based datacenters support demand for higher power UPS systems, prompting
                                                    vendors to expand UPS production capacity. We believe the combination of
                                                    stronger demand and competing resource requirements can strain available
                                                    engineering and manufacturing capabilities, increasing the appeal of qualified
                                                    ODM partners to supplement internal production. Voltronic’s customization
                                                    capabilities and flexible manufacturing position it to capture this opportunity.

                                                    Financial Analysis
                                                    Income statement – 2026E marks the earnings trough; online UPS drives
                                                    the recovery from 2027E
                                                    Voltronic delivered an 8.7% sales CAGR and 9.9% net profit CAGR over 2018-2025,
                                                    although earnings have become more volatile in recent years due largely to swings
                                                    in the inverter business. We forecast sales to decrease 1% y/y to NT$20.4bn in
                                                    2026E, before recovering 8% y/y and 7% y/y to NT$21.9bn and NT$23.4bn in
                                                    2027E and 2028E respectively. The key driver is the higher value online UPS.

                                                    We forecast online UPS sales to grow 10%/13%/10% y/y in 2026E/2027E/2028E,
                                                    lifting its sales contribution from 37% in 2025 to 44% by 2028E. Together with
                                                    offline UPS, we estimate UPS products to make up 72% of group sales in 2028E vs
                                                    2025’s 63%. Conversely, we forecast inverter sales to decline 27% y/y in 2026E and
                                                    remain broadly flat thereafter, reducing their sales contribution from 29% in 2025
                                                    to 18% in 2028E.

                                                    We expect gross margin to bottom at 27.1% in 2026E vs. 29.0% in 2025, reflecting
                                                    negative impact from material cost inflation and weaker inverter profitability.
                                                    Thereafter, we forecast gross margin to recover to 28.1% and 29.0% in 2027E and
                                                    2028E, supported by a richer online UPS mix and improving segment margins. We
                                                    estimate online UPS gross margin to increase from 30.8% in 2026E to 33.4% in
                                                    2028E driven rising contribution from high power online UPS, while its rising sales
                                                    mix could provide increasing contribution to group gross profits.

                                                    Operating leverage should further support profitability. Opex fell from 8.0% of sales
                                                    in 2025 to 7.4% in 2026E and could remain at 7.2% thereafter, while R&D
                                                    investment is maintained at 4.2% of sales. We therefore forecast OPM to recover
                                                    from 19.7% in 2026E to 20.9% and 21.8% in 2027E and 2028E.

                                                    We estimate net profit to decrease 18% y/y in 2026E, partly hampered by a larger
                                                    FX loss, before rebounding 28% y/y and 12% y/y in 2027E and 2028E. We forecast
                                                    EPS to register NT$33.00/NT$42.30/NT$47.25 in 2026E/2027E/2028E.

                                                    We attribute Voltronic’s earnings decline in 2025 and our forecast for a further
                                                    decline in 2026E to persistent inverter weakness and additional cost and supply
                                                    pressures. In 2025, adverse weather in Pakistan shortened the inverter peak
                                                    season and weakened demand, while intensifying Chinese competition pressured
                                                    pricing and profitability. The weakness extended into 2026E as the Middle East
                                                    conflict disrupted logistics and delayed shipments, alongside continued customers
                                                    destocking in Pakistan. In 1H26, RMB appreciation further weighed on margins.
                                                    Meanwhile, raw material shortages constrained shipments and higher metal and
                                                    key component prices eroded gross margins. We therefore forecast earnings to
                                                    decline 18% y/y in 2026E before improving 28% y/y in 2027E.

                                                                                            Balance Sheet – Asset light model and net cash suggest high returns
                                                                                            Voltronic maintains a relatively asset-light balance sheet with fixed assets making
                                                                                            up 24% of total assets in 2025 despite its sizable sales scale. We estimate the
                                                                                            company to remain in a net cash position throughout 2026-2028E. We forecast
                                                                                            cash and cash equivalent assets to account for 36-39% of total assets in 2026-
                                                                                            2028E while there are no meaningful short-term borrowings and long-term debt.

                                                                                            We forecast ROE to rise from 37% in 2025 to 40% in 2026E and 48% in 2027E. The
                                                                                            high ROE is not driven by financial leverage, but primarily by its asset-light
                                                                                            business model, strong operating margins and high capital distribution.

                                                                                            Voltronic also maintains high shareholder-return policy. We assume an 87% cash
                                                                                            dividend payout ratio through 2026-2028E, implying cash dividends of
                                                                                            NT$29/NT$37/NT$41 per share.
