                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Valuation Methodology and Risks
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     We value Voltronic using a forward target P/E of 25x our 2027E EPS to derive a
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     target price of NT$1,050, broadly in line with its long-term average forward P/E
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     since 2013. We believe forward P/E is appropriate given the company’s established
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     earnings base and the importance of product mix and operating leverage to its
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     profitability. Using 2027E EPS captures a fuller year of anticipated earnings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     recovery following the softer 2026E base, alongside the ongoing transition toward
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     online and higher power UPS. This also aligns our valuation with the earnings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     outlook investors are likely to focus on as the recovery progresses.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Our target multiple of 25x is supported by Voltronic’s competitive position in UPS
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     outsourcing. Its established relationship with western power vendors and ability to
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     accommodate high mix, low volume production creates a solid foundation for the
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     intact share gains, supporting the durability of its earnings and hence justify a
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     valuation broadly consistent with its historical average. Stronger evidence of power
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     rack commercialization and sustained UPS mix improvement could support a
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     further re-rating.

                                                    flow enables internally funded investment and reduces reliance on external
                                                    financing; and 3) the company has a strong balance sheet and has been in net cash
                                                    position.

                                                                                            Company Overview
                                                                                            Established in 2008 and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 2014, Voltronic
                                                                                            Power is a Taiwan-based design and manufacturing service (DMS) provider
                                                                                            specializing in uninterrupted power supplies (UPS) and power-conversion
                                                                                            products. The company is headquartered in Taipei and operates manufacturing
                                                                                            facilities in Taiwan, China and Vietnam, with approximately 5,000 employees.

                                                                                            Voltronic adopts a pure-play ODM business model and does not market products
                                                                                            under its own brand. This avoids direct competition with customers and has helped
                                                                                            the company establish long-term relationships with most global Tier-1 UPS
                                                                                            brands, as well as numerous regional brand owners.

                                                                                            The company provides customers with product design, R&D, sourcing,
                                                                                            manufacturing and system integration services, with a focus on high-mix,
                                                                                            relatively low-volume and customized products.

                                                                                            Voltronic’s core products include offline UPS systems ranging from 400VA to 3kVA
                                                                                            and on-line UPS systems ranging from 1kVA to 3MVA. The company has
                                                                                            progressively expanded from conventional single phase UPS products into three-
                                                                                            phase, high-power and modular UPS systems. It has also diversified into off-grid
                                                                                            and hybrid solar inverters, energy storage systems, and EV chargers.

                                                                                            In 2025, online UPS contributed 37% of group sales, offline UPS 26%, inverters
                                                                                            29% and others 8%. By geo, Asia accounted for 60% of group sales, followed by
                                                                                            Americas 22%, EU 16% and others 2%.

CPO: Optical scale-up is getting closer to reality. A 64-XPU CPO-enabled
compute-rack demonstration highlighted the potential for direct optical links
between accelerators. As 200G/lane electrical channels approach physical
limitations, optical scale-up will become more important, particularly for customized
XPUs. However, pluggagle optics should retain scale-out volume leadership given
advantages in serviceability and cost. Packaging yield, fiber alignment, and reliability
remain key commercialization challenges.

Advanced packaging: Moving beyond 2.5D. MediaTek highlighted custom ASIC
designs approaching 10x reticle size, arguing that 3.5D integration could deliver
approximately 10x better die-to-die energy efficiency versus conventional 2.5D
interconnects. Management expects increasing adoption over the next 3-5 years.

Valuation Methodology and Risks

                          AirTAC International (1590.TW)

                          Base case, 29x 2027e P/E. We believe this methodology better captures earnings growth
                          momentum for industrial automation component plays (market sentiment moves along
                          with business cycles). As the industry enters an up-cycle, we think applying a near-peak cycle
                          valuation of 29x P/E is reasonable given the stronger business outlook.

                          Risks to Upside

                             n Stronger macroeconomic climate in China
                             n Stronger-than-expected demand from industrial automation

                          Risks to Downside

                             n Sharper economic downturn in China
                             n Miniature linear guideway business development taking more time
                             n Larger-than-expected investment in new products but weaker-than-expected demand

                          Hiwin Technologies Corp. (2049.TW)

                          Base case, P/E. We think this valuation methodology better captures Hiwin's earnings growth
                          momentum, as its valuation tends to move with the business cycle. We apply a target multiple
                          of 38x to our 2027 EPS estimate. We view this multiple as justified by the 47% operating profit
                          CAGR we project for 2025-28.

                          Risks to Upside

                             n Stronger industrial automation demand pickup.
                             n Market share gains.
                             n Earlier-than-expected revenue contribution from humanoids.

                          Risks to Downside

                             n Weaker industrial automation demand.
                             n More pricing pressure.
                             n Market share loss.
                             n More broad-based impact on the global economy from geopolitical risks.

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Valuation Methodology and Risks

                          Delta Electronics Inc. (2308.TW)

                          Base case: P/E multiple of 30x based on average 2027-28 EPS. We believe our target multiple
                          is justified by the 63% earnings CAGR we estimate for 2025-28, implying a PEG of 0.5, versus
                          the stock's ~23x P/E and 23% earnings CAGR during 2022-25, which implied a PEG of 1.0.

                          Risks to Upside

                            n Faster-than-expected global economic growth
                            n Falling raw material prices
                            n Margin improvement

                          Risks to Downside

                            n Global economic slowdown
                            n Ongoing component supply tightness
                            n Rising raw material prices
                            n Margin contraction as a result of higher operating expenses or faster ASP erosion

is Wistron > Hon Hai > Quanta, based on upside to PT.

Key Takeaways
  We estimate GB200/300 rack output in September at ~6.5K (-23% m/m).

  Quanta shipped 1.55-1.60K GB200/GB300 racks.

  Wistron shipped 1.25-1.30K GB200/GB300 racks.

  Hon Hai shipped ~2.7K GB200/300 racks.

  We also introduce our 2027 forecast at 90.4K racks (+10% y/y).

We introduce 2027 forecast at 90.4K racks (+10% y/y) vs our 2026 forecast now
at 82K racks: This year is a strong one for downstream rack assemblers, with rack
shipments up ~209% y/y, but we expect rack shipments to grow another ~10% y/y
to reach 90.4K in CY27. For CY27, our forecast implies Hon Hai will be a share gainer
with rack share up to 43% (from 37% in CY26), with Quanta staying unchanged at
26% and Wistron's share up slightly to 24% (from 23% in CY26).

Quanta (2382.TW, OW): September revenue was NT$325.3B (-23% m/m, +77% y/y).
We attribute the m/m decline mainly to lower GB200/300 rack shipments at 1.55-
1.60K racks (-38% m/m), despite being offset slightly by higher NB shipments at
4.2M units (+62% m/m, -9% y/y). In 3Q, Quanta shipped ~6.2K racks (+3% q/q),
which came in slightly lower than our forecast of ~6.4K racks. Total 3Q revenue
reached ~NT$1,116M (+8% q/q, +125% y/y), which is 15% above MSe but in-line with
the Street. For 2026, we forecast Quanta to ship 20.9K racks, and we introduce our
preliminary 2027 forecast at 23.5K (+12% y/y).

In this report, we focus on preliminary JMTBA orders, which we                         Greater China Technology Hardware
                                                                                      Asia Pacific
believe could be a catalyst for AirTAC's and Hiwin's share prices.                    Industry View                   In-Line


According to the Japan Machine Tool Builders' Association (JMTBA), headline
orders grew 13% MoM and 60% YoY in September 2026 (vs. +2% MoM/+65%
YoY in August 2026), to ¥223bn.

    • Domestic orders were +24% MoM/+46% YoY (vs. -3% MoM/+62% YoY in
      August), at ¥64bn.
    • Overseas orders were +9% MoM/+67% YoY (vs. +5% MoM/+66% YoY in
      August), at ¥159bn.


Our view:

    • We think the sequential growth in overseas orders was consistent with
      seasonality, while the strength on a YoY basis continued to point to an
      upcycle scenario.
    • Within overseas orders, we think China and Europe may have outperformed,
      as manufacturing PMIs held up better (50.1/52.9 for China/Europe in
      September vs. 49.8/52.7 in August). N.A is likely to be softer compared to
      other regions, as its manufacturing PMI edged down slightly to 54.5 in
      September (vs. 54.6 in August).
    • We remain OW on both AirTAC (1590.TW) and Hiwin (2049.TW) as we see
      company-specific drivers on top of the industry recovery trend:
        ° Airtac should continue to benefit from its own market share gains, and
          valuation appears undemanding at 18x 2027e P/E (vs. 25x average since
            2020).
        ° Hiwin should see margin expansion in the coming quarters, driven by
          higher utilization and price hikes, which we believe could be share price
            catalysts. Current valuation of 29x 2027 P/E implies upside vs. peak
            cycle valuation at 35-40x P/E.                                            Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with

Valuation Methodology and Risks

                          AirTAC International (1590.TW)

                          Base case, 29x 2027e P/E. We believe this methodology better captures earnings growth
                          momentum for industrial automation component plays (market sentiment moves along
                          with business cycles). As the industry enters an up-cycle, we think applying a near-peak cycle
                          valuation of 29x P/E is reasonable given the stronger business outlook.

                          Risks to Upside

                             n Stronger macroeconomic climate in China
                             n Stronger-than-expected demand from industrial automation

                          Risks to Downside

                             n Sharper economic downturn in China
                             n Miniature linear guideway business development taking more time
                             n Larger-than-expected investment in new products but weaker-than-expected demand

                          Hiwin Technologies Corp. (2049.TW)

                          Base case, P/E. We think this valuation methodology better captures Hiwin's earnings growth
                          momentum, as its valuation tends to move with the business cycle. We apply a target multiple
                          of 38x to our 2027 EPS estimate. We view this multiple as justified by the 47% operating profit
                          CAGR we project for 2025-28.

                          Risks to Upside

                             n Stronger industrial automation demand pickup.
                             n Market share gains.
                             n Earlier-than-expected revenue contribution from humanoids.

                          Risks to Downside

                             n Weaker industrial automation demand.
                             n More pricing pressure.
                             n Market share loss.
                             n More broad-based impact on the global economy from geopolitical risks.

                                                       flooding to allow Delta to achieve a c.15% QoQ growth in 4Q26. Overall, we view the
                                                       demand as solid despite the supply headwind. As for the Section 337 investigation raised
                                                       by Vicor, we believe the impact would be limited at the end, but it still serves as proof that
                                                       the DC-DC module’s contribution would expand quickly again due to hyperscalers’ ASIC AI
                                                       servers in 2026 (like with the Hopper generation in 2023). As written in on our latest report
                                                       (Key beneficiary of the AI ASIC server trend, published 30 September, we believe this will
                                                       be a key growth driver for Delta in 2027. We have a Buy (1) rating on Delta, with a 12-
                                                       month TP of TWD3,088, based on a target PER of 49x applied to our 1-year forward EPS
                                                       forecast. Key downside risk: lower-than-expected demand.

power semiconductor supply and no further flooding to allow Delta to achieve a c.15%
QoQ growth in 4Q26. Overall, we view the demand as solid despite the supply headwind.

US ITC 337 investigation on behalf of Vicor (VICR):
• Fact: The US ITC has launched a Section 337 investigation following Vicor’s complaint
  alleging that the imported vertical power delivery systems, related components, and
  computing systems infringe its patent. Vicor is seeking a limited exclusion order and
  cease-and-desist orders to restrict imports and sales of the allegedly infringing products.

• Current investigation list:
  o Delta Electronics, Inc., Taipei, Taiwan
       ▪ Delta Electronics (Americas) Ltd., Fremont, California
       ▪ DET Logistics (USA) Corporation, Fremont, California
  o Infineon Technologies AG, Munich, Germany
  o Luxshare Precision Industry Co., Ltd., Dongguan, China
       ▪ Dongguan Luxshare Technology Co., Ltd. a/k/a Luxshare-Tech, Dongguan,
           China
  o Monolithic Power Systems, Inc., Kirkland, Washington
       ▪ Chengdu Monolithic Power Systems Co., Ltd., Chengdu, China
       ▪ MPS International (Shanghai) Ltd., Shanghai, China
  o Flex Ltd., Austin, Texas
  o Celestica Inc., Toronto, Canada
  o Quanta Computer Inc., Taoyuan City, Taiwan
       ▪ Quanta Cloud Technology Inc., Taoyuan City, Taiwan
       ▪ Quanta Cloud Technology USA LLC, San Jose, California
       ▪ Quanta Computer USA Inc., Fremont, California
  o Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. Ltd. (d/b/a Foxconn), New Taipei City, Taiwan
       ▪ Foxconn Industrial Internet Co. Ltd., Shenzhen, China
       ▪ FII USA Inc. (a/k/a Foxconn Industrial Internet USA Inc.) Milwaukee,
           Wisconsin
       ▪ Ingrasys Technology Inc., Taoyuan City, Taiwan
       ▪ Ingrasys Technology USA Inc., San Jose, California

• History:
  o 1st instance: 2023 July (Case number: 337-TA-1370; VICR won)
       ▪ Target product: Traditional power converter modules
       ▪ Target parent companies: Delta, Quanta, Hon Hai
  o 2nd instance: 2026 Feb (Case number: 337-TA-1484; ongoing)
       ▪ Target product: Certain power converters, circuit board assemblies, and
           computing systems
       ▪ Target parent companies: Delta, Luxshare, Monolithic Power Systems,
           Wistron, Wiwynn, Quanta

• What happens next: The USITC has not yet ruled on the merits of the case; an
  administrative law judge will hold an evidentiary hearing and issue an initial
  determination subject to Commission review, with a target completion date set within
  45 days of initiation (implied as 23 Nov). Any remedial orders would take effect upon
  issuance and become final after 60 days unless disapproved by the U.S. Trade
  Representative for policy reasons.

• Our-read: This is not the first time that Delta has had to face Vicor on power module
  competition. The first time was during the Hopper generation in 2023 when Nvidia was
  still adopting power modules within its AI servers. We think this investigation has to do


                              2
                                                            Delta Electronics (2308 TT)
                                                                               12 October 2026


  with the rising revenue contribution from Google’s AI server demand in 2026. For more
  details, please refer to Key beneficiary of the AI ASIC server trend, published on 30
  September. As we believe hyperscalers will still rely on Delta’s manufacturing and
  integration capabilities, we see limited chance that Delta’s products would be banned
  from this investigation. It is more likely that these two companies will settle in the end
  with Delta paying the licensing fee to Vicor, just as we have seen back in 2023. To us,
  the impact should be limited but it signals very strong end demand from hyperscalers
  again (like in 2023), which will be a key growth driver for Delta in 2027.

What we recommend:
We have a Buy (1) rating on Delta, with a 12-month TP of TWD3,088, based on a target
PER of 49x applied to our 1-year forward EPS forecast. Key downside risk: lower-than-
expected demand.

漢磊 3707 TT（電子-半導體）

AI 担注，終迎春燕

買進－中立轉買進
目標價：100.0 元　+21.6%
收盤價：82.2 元

投資與評價

1. AI 需求強勁、2H26 逐步復甦，SiC 競爭壓力減緩，去庫存亦已完成，預估 2026 年營收年增 29.0%。
2. 新增產能陸續開出，應用多點開花，產品價量齊升，預估 2027 年營收年增 23.8%。
3. 預估漢磊 2026/2027 年 EPS 為 0.99/4.77 元。考量整體產業趨勢顯著下，以同業本益比區間中間偏上位置 21 倍為評價基礎（21X FY27E EPS），目標價 100 元，由中立轉為買進投資建議。

重點更新

2026 年 Si 逐步回溫、化合物半導體需求跳升，預估營收年增 29.0%

根據調研，漢磊在六吋需求與產能利用率均有改善。四、五月時廠趨去產能利用率長期偏低，包含原物料取得不易。8 月已停止生產，10 月完成設備與人員轉移，將資源集中於高價值的六吋與八吋產品。在 Si 產品方面，TVS 受惠於新能源保護電路需求增加及精單效應，目前產能能庶?漢磊供應（目前時），推估 2H26 較 1H26 成長的 32%。化合物半導體部分，GaN 亦受惠 AI 資料中心需求，產能滿載，HoH 研究部推估成長 26%。目前客戶需求已達可供應量的兩倍水準。SiC 部分先前因大陸廠商競爭激烈，亦面臨去庫存，產能利用率上半年僅約三成水準，現因其他廠商減產以及去庫存完成，3Q26 已回升至六成。研究部預估 4Q26 將進一步回升至 65%水準。低基期下 2H26 營收與 HoH 將成長 123.5%，整體預估 2026 年營收全年增 29.0%。

AI 帶動 2027 年維持高速成長，預估營收年增 23.8%

TVS 部分由於新增產能陸續開出，加上 AI 伺服器、高速介面及晶片微縮後增加的靜電保護需求，預估 2027 年將成長 19.8%。GaN 應用由消費性快充擴大至 AI 伺服器 PSU、48V/800V 直流電源轉換架構，考量產能效率以及供應能力，在客戶需求維持強勁下，研究部預估 2027 年成長約 15%水準。至於 SiC 應用由電動車主驅逆變器，延伸至車載充電器。AI 資料中心的高功率 PSU 與固態變壓器部分客戶已在開發相關產品，在基期低下，明年 SiC 營收相較今年將翻倍成長。目前與世界先進合作的八吋的月產能約 1,500 片，漢磊自有六吋 SiC 月產能約 5,000 片，合計約 8,000 片六吋等效月產能。整體 2027 年研究部預估營收將年增 23.75%，達 92.1 億元。

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

                                              M&A Rank
                                              Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary
                                              across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring
                                              companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2
                                              representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard
                                              departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not
                                              factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

 Price objective basis & risk
Lotes (ZYZTF)
Our PO of NT$2,245 is based on 20x 2027E EPS. Our valuation multiple of 20x (2SD
above historical P/E trading average) reflects rising sales mix from better-margin server
business with ASP increase, double-digit sales/EPS CAGR in 2026-28, and solid balance
sheet. Our P/E multiple can also be justified by solid CPU server demand amid
accelerating agentic AI needs, Lotes' top position as desktop/server CPU socket supplier
to ride on Intel/AMD's ongoing desktop/server CPU platform upgrade.

Upside risks: (1) further ASP increase thanks to faster adoption/penetration of new
DT/server platform and new product, (2) faster progress in AI related business, (3) faster
AI PC launch/adoption, (4) GM upside from lowering/stabilizing raw material prices, and
(5) more favorable FX (USD/NTD and/or USD/RMB) movement to benefit GM and/or
non-operating items.

Downside risks: (1) slower ASP increase due to new CPU platform delay, (2) slower
progress from AI business, (3) weaker PC/server market demand amid inflation/macro
uncertainties, (4) GM pressure from higher raw material prices, (5) higher labor/logistics
cost from supply-chain disruption and uncertain China lockdown policy, (6) unfavorable
FX movement to weigh on GM and/or non-operating items, and (7) peers' more
aggressive pricing competition.

 Price objective basis & risk
Kinsus (KNSUF)
We set our PO at NT$1,450 based on 35x 2H27-1H28E P/E, which is at mid-to-high-end
level in its historical trading range (8-40x) since 2013. In our view, the multiple is backed
by ROE and operating margin recovery to 36% and 25% in 2027-28E (vs 8% and 10% in
2025-26E).

Upside risks to our PO are (1) tighter ABF supply, (2) increasing adoption of SiP and AiP,
(3) lower competition pressure and (4) slow development of alternative technology.

Downside risks are (1) greater ABF expansion from peers, (2) muted SiP/AiP adoption, (3)
more severe competition, and (4) unfavorable technology development.

 Price objective basis & risk
Unimicron (UMCRF)
Our PO of NT$1,650 is based on 35x 2H27-1H28E, which is roughly 1 standard deviation
above the historical average of 20x since 2017. In our view, the multiple is appropriate,
as we expect Unimicron's earnings to be supported by its high-end technology offerings,
where end market demand seems more resilient.

Upside risks are (1) tighter ABF supply, (2) greater PC and regular server demand, and (3)
lower competition pressure.

Downside risks are (1) greater ABF expansion from peers, (2) lower ASP content increase
at AI server, and (3) bigger drop in the demand of consumer electronic products.

大立光 3008 TT （電子-光電）

買進
目標價：7,950 元　+19.4%
收盤價：6,660 元

毛利築底、矽光接棒

投資與評價

1. 大立光 3Q26 雖受綠電成本大增影響，但獲利終見回升；預期 4Q26 仍處手機零組件拉貨旺季，獲利緩步回穩。

2. 高規旗艦手機產品持續開發並未停歇，27 年主鏡頭規格將再升級，整體手機銷售需求未見明顯衰退，且公司光纖陣列(FA)已通過客戶認證，並自 2H27 起 FAU 開始貢獻營運，26 年 EPS 163.99 元、27 年 EPS 189.78 元。

3. 目前股價約為 35.1X FY27E EPS，高於近 5 年本益比參考區間 10~48X 中間偏上位置，考量 3Q26 獲利回升、4Q26 仍處旺季使獲利回穩，維持買進投資評等。持續投入新興應用產品開發，跨出手機領域，包含雷射與共同封裝所需關鍵零組件，並預期於 27 年開始挹注營運，故將目標價調升至 7,950 元(42X 修正後 FY27E EPS)。

重點更新

大立光 3Q26 雖受綠電成本大增影響，但獲利終見回升

大立光 3Q26 進入手機零組件拉貨旺季，7 月營收自 6 月低基期回升，8 月未能延續成長力道，直至 9 月方見明顯放量，整體營收為 156.51 億元(+14.5% QoQ)，低於預估之 180.80 億元(+32.3% QoQ) 13.4%，主因為美系客戶對於新機系列拉貨趨於保守。除新機可變光圈鏡頭量產良率較原預期更低以外，綠電採購成本上升亦為主要壓力來源，毛利率 42.2%，低於預期，也因營收規模縮減，營業費用率由預估之 10.6%上揚至 12.0%，營業淨利 47.35 億元(-8.0% QoQ)，低於預期，但有匯兌收益挹注，稅後淨利 51.82 億元(+11.0% QoQ)，EPS 39.62 元，獲利終見回升。

預期大立光 4Q26 仍處手機零組件拉貨旺季，獲利緩步回升

大立光 4Q26 仍處手機零組件拉貨旺季，產能稼動率維持滿載，美系客戶於 1H27 發表之新機也自 10 月啟動拉貨，預期 10 月拉貨動能與 9 月相當、11 月拉貨轉趨保守而出現下滑，故下修整體營收預估 15.9%至 170.06 億元(+8.7% QoQ)。因 3Q26 起增加之綠電成本，即使可變光圈鏡頭良率逐步改善，仍未完全回復至正常水準，調降毛利率預估至與 3Q26 相近之 42.1%，維持與原預估相近之營業費用 19.22 億元(+2.7% QoQ)，營業淨利預估為 52.40 億元(+10.7% QoQ)，稅後淨利仍可季增 5.6%至 54.74 億元，EPS 41.85 元，獲利緩步回升。

頎邦 6147 TT （電子-半導體）

金光領航，頎勢如虹

強力買進－初評強力買進

目標價：315.0元　+39.4%
收盤價：226.0元

投資與評價

1. 頎邦3Q26受惠美系手機新機備貨，加上1.6T光通訊TIA與PD訂單放量，推升營收及毛利率；預期4Q26手機DDIC相關需求季節性放緩，惟光通訊訂單持續成長，Modulator量產及TFLN新案導入支撐營運。

2. 頎邦26年受惠光通訊金凸塊訂單放量，EPS 6.03元；27年1.6T光通訊需求成長，TFLN量產與測試業務擴張，光通訊相關營收佔比達兩成，加上韓系DDIC轉單挹注，推升營運，EPS 10.52元。

3. 目前頎邦股價交易在226.0元(21.5X 27(F) PER)，位於近三年參考本益比區間18~42x區間下緣位置，考量頎邦在金凸塊製程具備技術與產能優勢，加上測試與切割業務擴張有望提高單片晶圓加工產值，給予平均值30倍本益比與強力買進投資建議，目標價315.0元(30X 27(F) PER)。

重點更新

頎邦3Q26光通訊與美系手機新機需求雙引擎帶動營運創近四年新高

頎邦3Q26受惠於美系手機品牌大廠新機備貨需求帶動OLED DDI及RF相關金凸塊業務成長，加上AI資料中心持續升級至1.6T光收發模組，帶動單通道200G相關TIA及PD金凸塊需求增加，預估頎邦3Q26營收75.82億元(+14.3% QoQ)。高毛利率的光通訊業務營收占比提升，且整體產能利用率改善，預估毛利率31.9%(+1.6pts QoQ)。光通訊新產品開發、測試技術導入費用增加，預估營業利益16.41億元(+28.4% QoQ)，稅後淨利15.56億元(+63.8% QoQ)，EPS 2.10元，營運創近四年新高。

預期頎邦4Q26 DDIC需求季節性放緩，光通訊與TFLN新業務支撐營運

頎邦4Q26 OLED DDI及RF相關需求季節性放緩，惟光通訊業務持續受惠於200G/lane金凸塊需求成長，加上國內晶圓代工大廠旗下的特殊製程業者TFLN預計於4Q26開始貢獻於時，國內晶圓代工大廠八吋TFLN也將開始貢獻，且我們推測TFLN從金凸塊到Testing、Dicing都會交給頎邦，故ASP會大幅提高。預估頎邦4Q26營收75.02億元(-1.1% QoQ)。雖光通訊營收占比提升但DDIC產能利用率因季節性需求放緩而下降，加上新產品導入初期的相關成本，預估毛利率31.4%(-0.6pts QoQ)。隨光通訊測試及封裝相關技術持續開發，且新產品認證及研發投入增加，預估營業費用為8.40億元(+7.7% QoQ)，稅後淨利15.32億元(-1.5% QoQ)，EPS 2.06元。

9 月營收優於預期

投資與評價

1. 長興 9 月營收達 44.3 億元，佔比我們先前預估 3Q26 營收 121.51 億元的 36%，優於我們先前預估。
2. 7～9 月營收合計為 125.96 億元，亦優於我們預估。
3. 公司獲利持續上升，且跨入半導體領域奠定其評價表現，研究部維持買進投資建議，目標價 90 元，以 22x FY27 獲利預估。

重點更新

9 月營收優於我們先前預估

長興 9 月營收達 44.3 億元（MoM +8.9%、YoY +29.4%），高於我們先前預估 42.0 億元約 5.5%，優於我們預估。7～9 月營收合計為 125.96 億元，亦優於我們預估 3Q26 營收 121.51 億元。綜觀各業務營運，9 月合成樹脂業務達 20.97 億元，月增達 11%，研究部推估主要係因油價上漲帶動產品報價；電子材料業務達 10.2 億，月減約 5%，長慶營收持平；特用材料 12.0 億元，月增約 19%；半導體材料營收達 1.4 億元，月增約 26%，WCMC 產能放量推動 MUF 膠需求。

長慶 9 月營收維持於 8 月高水平

長慶 9 月營收為 3.64 億元（MoM +1.2%、YoY +220.3%），高於我們先前預估 3.0 億元約 21%。7～9 月營收合計為 9.08 億元，亦優於我們先前預估 3Q26 營收 7.21 億元。長慶月營收自 8 月開始跳升，9 月維持高水平，我們認為主要係因於 2H26 進入三段式設備認列高峰，產能逐漸開始出加大量產品組合轉佳帶來高成長。

4Q26 各業務持續轉佳，營運呈現季增

展望 4Q26，研究部認為在油價持續有撐下，合成樹脂業務產品報價將能持續維持於高檔水平；半導體材料將穩定放量，且有機會打入 CoWoS 等其他先進封裝技術平台，將大幅提升半導體材料業務想像空間；長慶營收將隨產能持續開出、產品組合轉佳而呈現季增，將能把握長興營收及獲利成長。預估 FY26/27 EPS 分別為 2.66 元/4.17 元，YoY +88.4%/+56.9%，公司獲利持續上升，且跨入半導體領域奠定其評價表現，維持買進投資建議，目標價 90 元，以 22x FY27 獲利預估。

              (Parallel Micro-Lens Array)：可使目標面形成多點聚焦能量集中；3) V-Groove：被用作光纖定位
              的載體，精準放置對準光纖確保耦合；傳統 V-Groove 困境在於 CPO 光通訊對精度要求極高(誤差
              須小於 0.3 μm；相當於頭髮的 1/300)，傳統作法依賴進口完美 V-Groove，因材料本身公差加上光
              纖公差，累計誤差常大於 1 μm，大立光透過自主開發的自動化機台與製程補償技術，可將不完美
              的 V-Groove 及不完美的光纖組成最終總誤差控制在 0.3 μm 以下的 FA。

光所生產的光學鏡片組(Optical Lens)占手機鏡頭模組價值比重 19%。大立光目前於台灣共有 13 個廠區，中國則有蘇州廠

  ESG 分析

分別藉由「在 ESG 議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG 上的表現。

► ESG 總分： 大立光整體的 ESG 風險評級屬於中等風險，於 Sustainalytics 資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名亦排行於前段的
   位置，在電子零組件行業中的公司中排名亦略為領先同業。

► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 大立光的整體風險敞口較低，且略低於細分行業平均。「原料使用」、「商業道德」以及「排
   放物、廢水與廢棄物」是值得關注的實質 ESG 議題。公司面臨的商業道德風險主要源自於其價值鏈中的業務關係，以
   及其業務所在國家和企業規模。

► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：大立光（Largan）在 ESG 領域表現出色，尤其在環境政策方面表現強勁，並具備極
   高的 ESG 報告標準。公司由董事會或執行委員會負責監督 ESG 治理，彰顯了高層問責機制。其舉報機制尚屬完善，但
   在員工保護和報告流程方面仍有改善空間。

ESG 圖表定義
項目                  定義                                                                              說明
                    直接與間接能源消耗總量(十億焦耳)
                    - 公司運營範圍內消耗之能源總量
                    - 能源使用總量 = 直接能源消耗總量 + 間接能源消耗量
能源使用                - 總能源使用量包括購買的能源、生產的能源
                    - 就公用事業而言，輸電/電網損耗為其業務活動之一部分，被視為總能源消耗，數據不包括
                    為滿足能源使用而生產的電力（公用事業為出售而生產）
                    - 就公用事業而言，用於能源生產的煤、天然氣或核能等原料不屬於「總能源使用」項下
                    Primary 再生能源購買總量(十億焦耳)
                    - 公司各種來源之能源消耗量與購買的能源中屬於自然界可再生者（太陽能、風能、水能、
購買之再生能源
                    生物質能、地熱能）之量
                    - 如無證據顯示再生能源由公司生產，則所報告的能源數據視為購買的再生能源
再生能源使用率             再生能源占總能源消耗量之比例
                    直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量(公噸)
                    - 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量）
CO2 約當排放量
                    - 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化
                    合物 (PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3)
                    直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量（公噸）銷售（百萬元）比
                    - 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量）
CO2 約當排放量營收比
                    - 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化
                    合物 (PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3)
                    廢棄物總量(公噸)
                    - 總廢棄物 = 無害廢棄物 + 有害廢棄物
廢棄物總量               - 僅考慮固體廢棄物，但如液體廢棄物以公噸為單位呈報，則會將其加入求得包含液體廢棄
                    物之總量
                    - 對於採礦、石油與天然氣等行業，tailings、廢石、煤、飛灰等廢棄物亦考慮在內
                    公司呈報的廢棄物回收率
                    - 廢棄物回收率 = 廢棄物回收量/總廢棄物*100
廢棄物回收率
                    - 廢棄物轉化為能源或經由廢棄物焚燒產生能源視為廢棄物回收
                    - 經由堆肥回收的廢棄物視為回收之廢棄物
                    總取水量(立方公尺)
總取水量                - 由呈報組織直接或經水公司等中介機構從任何水源抽取的總水量
                    - 水井、城鎮/公用事業/市政用水、河水、地表水等不同之水源均予以考慮
                    環保支出總金額
環保支出                - 所有用於環境保護，或防止、減少、控制環境因素、影響、危害的投資與支出，亦包括處
                    置、處理、衛生、清理支出
                    員工流動率
                    - 包括任何原因（自願或非自願）離開公司的員工，如辭職、退休、自然離職/死亡、醫療失
                    能、冗員、裁員、重組、解僱、裁減或定期合約到期
員工流動率
                    - 員工流動率 =（離開之員工/平均員工人數）*100
                    - 平均員工人數 =（本年末員工人數 + 去年末員工人數）/2
                    - 本財年末員工數 =上個財年末員工數 + 新員工數 - 離開之員工數
                    女性經理百分比
                    - 女性經理占公司經理的百分比
女性經理
                    - 如有不同階層之百分比，如最高階、高階、中階、初階，則會考慮中階女性經理之百分比
                    - 女性經理百分比 = 女性經理人數/經理總數*100
                    女性員工百分比
女性員工                - 女性員工占公司員工總數的百分比
                    - 女性員工百分比 = 女性人數/員工總數*100
                    所有員工教育訓練總時數
                    - 僅考慮員工教育訓練時數
教育訓練總時數             - 包括一般員工所有類型的教育訓練（如健康與安全、環境、急難事件救援、技能與職業發
                    展）
                    - 如果數據以天為單位，則乘以 8，係假設 1 天 = 8 小時工作
每位員工教育訓練時數          平均每年每位員工總教育訓練時數

                                   Our net income estimates are revised by -13% / -4% / +16% in 2026-28E mainly on
                                   changes in revenues, GM, and Opex ratio, reflecting: (1) handset lens: we continue to
                                   expect Largan’s lens pixel mix upgrade, but at a slower pace, reflecting the 3Q26 miss
                                   and slow smartphone market amid high memory costs, (2) FAU: we estimate revenue
                                   contribution will begin in 2H27, with 0.6m / 5m in 2027 / 28E, along with product mix
                                   upgrade toward higher bandwidth FAU that should support ASP and GM. We expect FAU
                                   revenue contribution of 3% in 2027E and exceed 50% in 2030E, (3) GM: we lower our
                                   GM estimates to reflect the slower pace of handset lens pixel mix upgrade and the
                                   company’s higher costs on green energy. We expect GM to sustain at ~50% in 2026-28E,
                                   supported by continuous handset lens pixel mix upgrade and strong demand of FAU, (4)
                                   Opex ratio: we continue to expect rising opex, while the opex ratio would improve as
                                   strong revenue growth driven by FAU and FAU’s higher ASP relative to handset lens
                                   enhance operating efficiency.

GS Factor Profile
The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs
for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

M&A Rank
Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary
across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring
companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2
representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard
departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not
factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

WinWay Technology  6515.TW 6515 TT

EQUITY: OSAT

Be mindful of transition period

Late-stage product cycle and likely transition gap temper 4Q outlook; retain Buy on intact L-T view

Maintain Buy; TP lowered to TWD8,250, implying 49.5% upside

WinWay’s share price corrected ~35% in July (TWSE down 8%), mainly on its GM miss in 2Q26 (results note). The share price has fluctuated over the past two months, with periodic upward momentum, particularly following the release of strong July/August revenue figures in early Aug/ early Sep. However, the stock hit its limit down on 7 Oct, following a 27% m-m decline in Sep revenue and a 3Q26 revenue miss (+29% q-q vs. NMR/BBG’s +35-40% q-q). We expect revenue momentum to naturally moderate, as some key probe card projects enter the later stages of their shipment cycle. However, the strength in the socket segment appears insufficient to fully offset the slowdown in the probe card segment. For 4Q, we revise our revenue forecast from single-digit q-q growth to a mid-to-high single-digit q-q decline (vs. BBG expectation of single-digit q-q growth), as our earlier estimates were based primarily on capacity expansion assumptions. We have since refined our projections to incorporate actual project shipping patterns. While 4Q is likely to be a product transition period for both sockets and probe cards from one major XPU vendor — with new project ramps scheduled for next year — we do see other key ASIC/XPU projects ramp gradually. We thus slightly cut 2026F EPS by 4%, and still expect 2027-28F revenue to grow ~70% y-y, respectively. Based on our revised earnings, we lower TP from TWD9,000 to TWD8,250, still on 32x 2027-28F EPS. We reaffirm Buy considering the broad project base and intact mid-to-long term outlook, on top of its solid share in key customer programs, in our view. The stock currently trades at 21.4x.

Implications from key AI XPU to relevant supply chain names

Since late 2025, we have observed a slower-than-expected ramp for one key AI XPU, due to memory/thermal issues. We recently observed further hiccups. While WinWay delivered test interfaces for the new chips on schedule this year, the end device’s ramping trajectory may also potentially influence customer procurement behavior/ repeat orders going forward. We believe a challenging transition period is consistent with our recent earnings cuts for KYEC (2449 TT, Buy). A failure to resolve the technical issues in a timely manner could pose additional downside risk to the ramp and, in turn, impact our forecasts. That said, near-term ramping difficulties or schedule delays may weigh on the results (and share price), but these appear to be timing-related rather than a fundamental shift in underlying demand.

Key Takeaways

■ 3Q26 gross margin is 42.2%, which is lower-than-expected and triggers a 31-36% GP and OP miss vs. our estimates.

■ Revenue is likely to be flat MoM in October and decline sequentially in November.

■ CPO-related (FAU) has seen good progress with new product verification passed.

Largan reported 3Q26 net income of NT$5.182bn, down 27% YoY.

The company reported a 11% YoY revenue decline, to NT$15.651bn; gross margin declined YoY and QoQ to 42.2% in 3Q26, lower than expected due to lower new-project yields and structural green electricity cost hikes.

Management expects shipments to be flat MoM in October and decline sequentially in November as order momentum is weaker-than-expected.

FAU/CPO development well on track: First FA project passed customer verification; expanding from FA into FAU, including coupling and potential FAU-to-carrier assembly, with a dedicated new facility expected to support mass production from around mid-2027. We maintain our long-term positive view on Largan’s FAU/CPO opportunities.

（+1,587.1% YoY）

                                                                聯友金屬 7610 TT
非中鎢供應鏈稀缺性提升
中國鎢出口限制使國際供應持續偏緊，聯友藉二次硬質合金回收與濕法冶金技術，受惠國際客戶
加速建立非中供應鏈，2026 年鎢價上漲、自售比重提升及屏東二廠新增產能開出，帶動獲利明
顯成長；2027 年成長動能則由格進一步轉向產能擴張與產品高值化，隨屏南三廠及屏科廠新產
能陸續開出，產品由鎢酸鈉延伸至 APT、氧化鎢、鎢粉及碳化鎢，自售部分有機會在 2027 年挑
戰 60%。預估 2026/27 EPS 為 83.77/109.27 元。3. 目前股價評價位於近兩年本益比 10～24
倍區間中段，考量非中鎢供應鏈稀缺性、自售比重提升及 2027 年新產能接棒，給予區間中間偏
上的 22 倍 FY27E PER，給予強力買進評等，目標價 2,400 元(22x FY27E EPS)。


產業概況
鎢金屬需求持續由工業與國防驅動
2026 年中國鎢總供給約 8.51 萬噸 W、YoY +12.4%，其中原生礦約 4.36 萬噸、幾乎零成長，回
收鎢則由高價刺激增加約 50%至約 3.0 萬噸，使回收料占供給由 2025 年的 25–26%升至約 35%；
換言之 2026 幾乎所有可快速增加的供給彈性都來自回收處理，使得非新礦山供應的競爭也明顯
升高。顯示高鎢價已開始抑制價格敏感度較高的傳統用途，但切削工具、航太與國防等剛性需求
仍維持成長。全球鎢需求主要仍來自硬質合金，應用於切削工具、礦山鑽頭、汽車與精密加工；
其中礦業與營建約占 2025 年全球 WC 市場 38.5%。
國防需求的重要性在 2026 年進一步提高，美國與以色列對伊朗軍事行動、俄烏戰爭持續消耗飛
彈與穿甲彈用鎢，這類用途與硬質合金不同，使用後無法回收，使其對原生鎢形成永久性消耗。
因全球每年鎢需求約 10～11 萬噸，其中原生礦約占 65%、回收料約 35%，現有需求須依賴二
次資源補足。短期新礦與冶煉產能建置時間長，因此即使高價刺激新增供給，供需緊張仍不容易
快速逆轉。
各應用來看硬質合金(Cemented carbide)佔比最大，主要用於切削刀具、採礦鑽頭、耐磨零件與
國防彈藥等。加工材/材加工品（Mill products）
                            ：如鎢絲、鎢棒、鎢板等。鋼鐵與合金（Steel &
alloys）用於高速鋼、耐熱合金鋼等。化學品（Chemicals）
                                 ：催化劑、顏料及化學試劑。其中 PCB
鑽針需求在近年也快速增加，據估計因 AI server PCB 變得更厚、更多層、更難鑽，高速低損耗
材料使 WC 鑽針磨耗大幅提高。AI server PCB 已朝 28–46 層甚至更高層數發展，而一般鑽針
原本約可加 工 3,000 孔，在高階材料下可能降到約 600 孔，在相同鑽孔量可能需要接近 4–5 倍
鑽針消耗。半導體需求在 4Q26 仍然偏強，其中第一類是半導體製程本身使用的高純度鎢/WF₆
等材料，另一類是晶圓、封裝、設備與零組件加工所使用的 WC 超硬工具。整體而言隨著 AI
GPU/ASIC、HBM 與先進封裝擴產，使高純度 W 與精密 WC 工具需求維持穩定成長。
圖 3：鎢金屬主要應用

                                                                     聯友金屬 7610 TT
中國七成產能限制鎢出口影響大
全球鎢供應高度集中，在 2025 年全球鎢精礦開採產量約 8 萬多噸，中國占約 75%，且中國同時
掌握從礦山、APT、鎢粉到碳化鎢的完整加工鏈，鎢的供應風險除了礦源集中，更包含中游精煉
能力集中。2H25 開始中國開始收緊鎢礦開採配額並實施出口管制後，非中國市場供給明顯轉緊，
價格也顯著提升。
全球鎢市場主要依賴中國供應，因此中國價格大致主導全球定價；但出口限制與供應鏈安全政策
出現後，國際買家開始建立中國以外的礦源、冶煉及回收體系，使得國際報價持續走高，鎢回收
目前約占全球供給三成，雖然產地來源風險較低，但是既有供應鏈的產能瓶頸，使得回收流程取
得鎢的價格持續走高。雖陸續有些新礦場宣告將投入開發，但仍需兩年以上時間準備，舊有礦場
的重啟也面臨到回收率與經濟性的挑戰，且對於環境衝擊高未必適合歐美國家，目前最為環保與
的作法仍是從回收鎢開始加工。透過廢鎢回收陸續轉化為鎢酸鈉、APT、氧化鎢、鎢粉、碳化鎢，
將有利於賣方市場的精鍊供應商，邁向更高值化的末端產品發展。

美國積極多元化鎢礦來源
3Q26 美國政府承諾向 Elmet Group 投入 US$450mn，並搭配 DLA 最高 US$2bn 鎢戰略庫存
採購，政策目標已從單純取得礦源轉向礦山+APT/精煉+零組件的垂直整合。US$450mn 投資將
用於擴張美國鎢製造能力、取得長期原料、投資美國及盟國礦山與建立新的 refining/conversion
能力；其中初期資金約 US$200mn。另一方面 DLA 與 Elmet 簽訂最高 US$2bn IDIQ 合約，最
低保證採購 US$150mn，品項直接涵蓋鎢礦、鎢精礦及鎢酸鈉；Elmet 待新增礦山、offtake 與
processing capacity 形成後才向戰略庫存交貨，以避免政府囤貨擠壓既有民間供應。 EQ
Resources 規劃向美國供應 4,000 噸鎢精礦；但 Nevada APT processing facility 全面恢復營運
預計要到 2H28，因此 4Q26 政策首先增加的是戰略採購與長約需求，而非立即增加 APT 現貨供
給。這代表短期甚至可能強化非中國的原料競爭，但預計要數年後後才有機會逐步改善美國中游
加工缺口。

鈷金屬供給仍有短缺風險
2025 年全球鈷礦產量約 31 萬噸，其中剛果民主共和國約 23 萬噸、占七成比重，全球約 50%儲
量亦集中於剛果，而中國又掌握全球七成以上鈷精煉能力，因此上游礦源與中游精煉均高度集中。
需求方面 2025 年全球鈷消費動力電池占比超過 65%，EV 仍是最大需求來源；雖電池高鎳化、
低鈷化以及 LFP 滲透率提升，會限制單位電池鈷用量成長，但 IT 電池的使用仍以氧化鈷為主要
材料。而長期更值得注意的是航空發動機、燃氣渦輪、國防設備所使用的高溫合金，以及硬質合
金與高性能磁鐵需求。高溫合金目前約占鈷需求 15～20%，工業工具、硬質合金與催化劑約一
成，使鈷逐漸從單一新能源金屬轉變成兼具新能源與戰略材料屬性的關鍵金屬；在供應集中及可
追溯要求提高下，循環再生鈷、高純度鈷粉與非中國精煉能力的戰略價值亦將持續提高。


公司簡介
聯友金屬不依賴原生鎢礦，而是以廢硬質合金、鎢鋼及研磨屑等二次料作為鎢來源，經濕式冶金
回收後製成鎢酸鈉（Sodium Tungstate）
                         ，同時回收鈷，形成 WC/鎢鋼廢料、鎢酸鈉、APT、氧
化鎢的城市礦山供應鏈。公司目前鎢酸鈉年產能約 6,000 噸，2025 年鎢酸鈉出貨約 4,728 噸、
YoY +8%，其中代工約占 52%、自售約 48%，相較 2024 年代工 42%、自售 58%，可看出自
有設備利用率已處相對高檔；公司規劃透過新廠將鎢酸鈉產能進一步提高至約 12,000 噸/年、較
現有產能增加 100%，若以鎢酸鈉 Na₂WO₄·2H₂O 含鎢重量約 55.7%換算，滿產相當於一年可處
理約 6,700 噸 W contained。公司並規劃進一步向下游 APT 與氧化鎢延伸，使產品由目前以鎢
酸鈉為主，逐步建立回收料、鎢酸鈉、APT、WO₃的垂直整合能力。

ESG 政策

公司在社會面評分上屬中上，然而需在經濟與環境面與揭露面強化:
經濟面: 股東權益方面，公司優點為董事長親自出席股東常會；股東會結束後公開揭露逐項議案
之詳細表決資訊。公司可加強處為當年度未召開 2 次以上法人說明會。
法規遵循方面，公司於題項評估期間未有不合理或受主管機關處分之情事。獨立董事方面，公司
優點為至少 2 名獨立董事之連續任期不超過 9 年。公司可加強處為獨立董事席次未達董事席次
二分之一以上。董事會永續治理方面，公司優點為有設置永續發展相關委員會；有制訂環境、社
會及治理之中長期發展策略；當年度永續報告書經董事會通過。公司可加強處為負責永續發展之
最終負責人非董事長或總經理。董事會績效與薪酬方面，公司優點為將董事績效評估與薪資報酬
連結。公司可加強處為企業永續績效尚未與高階主管及董事薪酬進行連結。
董事會多元性方面，公司優點為揭露董事會多元化政策並揭露落實情形；董事會成員具備不同專
業背景。公司可加強處為任一性別董事席次未達 1/3。永續創新方面，公司優點為取得綠色認證。
公司可加強處為未揭露綠色相關部門設置情形與職責；未揭露綠色/永續採購之政策或金額。
此外，產業創新方面，公司優點為對其專利之智慧財產權進行管理與保護，並揭露量化績效。
法規遵循方面，公司近 3 年並未受公平交易委員會懲罰。


環境面: 環境系統與治理方面，公司優點為積極將綠色概念融入營運過程，打造綠色價值鏈；榮
獲 ISO 14001 環境管理認證；將環境管理作為與聯合國永續發展目標(SDGs)連結。空氣管理方
面，公司優點為制定空氣管理政策、揭露空氣汙染排放數據；公司可加強處為未揭露量化空氣汙
染減量目標。法規遵循方面，評估期間未違反空氣汙染相關法規或已針對違反情形提出具體改善
措施。氣候變遷管理方面，公司可加強處為未說明董事會或管理階層對氣候變遷議題之監督頻率
或事項；未揭露使用具公信力的 1.5 °C 以下及 3 °C 以上溫度情境評估氣候風險；未揭露與供
應鏈或合作夥伴共同推動因應氣候變遷相關策略；未揭露氣候變遷對公司所產生的機會項目。
溫室氣體管理方面，公司優點為揭露至少三年的溫室氣體範疇一與二排放量，並揭露涵蓋範圍或
佔營收比率。公司可加強處為未揭露溫室氣體管理專責單位及相關管理政策；未揭露範疇三排放
量；未揭露量化溫室氣體減量目標；未揭露是否通過碳盤查認證。節能管理方面，公司優點為揭
露用電或節能數據。公司可加強處為未揭露能源管理專責單位及相關管理政策；未揭露節能量化
目標；未揭露能源風險對營運的影響評估結果。再生能源管理方面，公司可加強處為未揭露再生
能源管理專責單位及相關推動政策；未揭露再生能源使用量或發電量；未揭露量化再生能源發展
目標。廢水管理方面，公司優點為制定廢水管理政策、揭露廢污水排放量；公司可加強處為未揭
露量化廢汙水減量目標。
揭路面: ESG 揭露方面，公司優點為依據 GRI 準則編寫永續報告書；於永續報告書清楚說明揭露
範疇；建置英文網站，並包含財務、業務及公司治理相關資訊；於永續報告書揭露重大性分析細
節。公司可加強處為永續報告書未依據 SASB 進行對應揭露；未上傳英文版永續報告書於公開資
訊觀測站；永續報告書尚未經過第三方機構確信或保證；未於官網揭露利害關係人問卷，供利害
關係人回饋；未說明公司營運對應 SDGs 目標之具體作為；未揭露使用雙重重大性分析重大性議
題。

       漲價效益持續發酵，4Q26 毛利率續升 : 公司今年 5～6 月起陸續與客戶進行漲
       價協商，並依客戶、產品及訂單狀況逐步反映，且主要針對新接訂單，因此漲
       價效益並非立即反映於營收及毛利率。隨 9～10 月開始陸續 出 貨 漲價後 訂 單 ，
       產品組合持續優化，漲價效益可望逐步挹注毛利率；我們認為由於 9 月營收已
       大致反映前一波漲價，加上新增產能尚未完全開出，預期 10～11 月營收維持
       相 對 穩 定 ， 惟 產 品 組 合 持 續 優 化 ， 漲 價 效 益 仍 可 帶 動 毛 利 率 進 一 步 提 升 。 12
       月營收則仍將受到年度盤點及聖誕假期等季節性因素影響而略有波動，但在高
       毛利產品占比提升及漲價效益持續發酵下，獲利率可望維持高檔，因此我們上
       調 4Q26 營收至 11.1 億元，毛利率至 41.89%，EPS 為 2.1 元。

       2027 年不只量增，更有望迎來價增 :我們認為光頡的高階精密電阻供需緊張格
       局至少延續至 2027 年，除目前部分產品交期仍較過去延長數週、訂單能見度
       已達 2027 年下半年外，高規格產品具較高製程及良率門檻，新供應商短期亦
       難以補足供給。從海外同業 Vishay 近期動態亦可觀察到類似趨勢，公司 2026
       年持續推動價格調整，且部分漲價已逐步反映於財務表現，反映高階電阻供應
       緊張並非單一供應商現象，而是產業供需結構正在改變。

       在需求持續高於供給的環境下，我們認為 2027 年漲價仍具延續空間，且價格
       將逐漸成為客戶取得產能的重要條件，後續調價未必採全面性調整，而可能與
       採購量及產能配置連動。另一方面，光頡新增產能並非單純追求出貨量，而將
       優先配置至高規格、高毛利及價格接受度較高的產品，意味著公司可望同時受
       惠於 ASP 提升及產品組合優化。我們因此認為， 2027 年光頡的獲利成長除了
       來自 AI 需求與產能擴充，漲價及高階產品占比提升將是毛利率與 EPS 進一步
       上修的重要驅動力。

       評價收斂不改獲利上修趨勢，維持買進 : 我們重申光頡買進評等，並上調
       2026/2027 年 EPS 預估至 5.57 元/11.13 元，反映 AI 伺服器放量帶動高階精密
       電阻需求，及交期拉長推升漲價效益，帶動產品組合與獲利能力改善。考量漲
       價效益已逐步反映，後續獲利成長將轉由 AI 需求及產品升級驅動，我們將評
       價基準由原先 2H26～1H27 EPS 調整至 2027 年 EPS，並參考 Vishay 目前約 20
       ～25 倍本益比，將合理本益比由 30 倍下修至 20 倍。

       漲價效益持續發酵，4Q26 毛利率續升 : 公司今年 5～6 月起陸續與客戶進行漲
       價協商，並依客戶、產品及訂單狀況逐步反映，且主要針對新接訂單，因此漲
       價效益並非立即反映於營收及毛利率。隨 9～10 月開始陸續 出 貨 漲價後 訂 單 ，
       產品組合持續優化，漲價效益可望逐步挹注毛利率；我們認為由於 9 月營收已
       大致反映前一波漲價，加上新增產能尚未完全開出，預期 10～11 月營收維持
       相 對 穩 定 ， 惟 產 品 組 合 持 續 優 化 ， 漲 價 效 益 仍 可 帶 動 毛 利 率 進 一 步 提 升 。 12
       月營收則仍將受到年度盤點及聖誕假期等季節性因素影響而略有波動，但在高
       毛利產品占比提升及漲價效益持續發酵下，獲利率可望維持高檔，因此我們上
       調 4Q26 營收至 11.1 億元，毛利率至 41.89%，EPS 為 2.1 元。

       2027 年不只量增，更有望迎來價增 :我們認為光頡的高階精密電阻供需緊張格
       局至少延續至 2027 年，除目前部分產品交期仍較過去延長數週、訂單能見度
       已達 2027 年下半年外，高規格產品具較高製程及良率門檻，新供應商短期亦
       難以補足供給。從海外同業 Vishay 近期動態亦可觀察到類似趨勢，公司 2026
       年持續推動價格調整，且部分漲價已逐步反映於財務表現，反映高階電阻供應
       緊張並非單一供應商現象，而是產業供需結構正在改變。

       在需求持續高於供給的環境下，我們認為 2027 年漲價仍具延續空間，且價格
       將逐漸成為客戶取得產能的重要條件，後續調價未必採全面性調整，而可能與
       採購量及產能配置連動。另一方面，光頡新增產能並非單純追求出貨量，而將
       優先配置至高規格、高毛利及價格接受度較高的產品，意味著公司可望同時受
       惠於 ASP 提升及產品組合優化。我們因此認為， 2027 年光頡的獲利成長除了
       來自 AI 需求與產能擴充，漲價及高階產品占比提升將是毛利率與 EPS 進一步
       上修的重要驅動力。

       評價收斂不改獲利上修趨勢，維持買進 : 我們重申光頡買進評等，並上調
       2026/2027 年 EPS 預估至 5.57 元/11.13 元，反映 AI 伺服器放量帶動高階精密
       電阻需求，及交期拉長推升漲價效益，帶動產品組合與獲利能力改善。考量漲
       價效益已逐步反映，後續獲利成長將轉由 AI 需求及產品升級驅動，我們將評
       價基準由原先 2H26～1H27 EPS 調整至 2027 年 EPS，並參考 Vishay 目前約 20
       ～25 倍本益比，將合理本益比由 30 倍下修至 20 倍。

MEMO


       3Q26 revenue: roughly in line

                                            Summary: Jentech reported September 2026 revenue of TWD3,054m (-5.3% MoM and
                                            +80.0% YoY; +47.1% YoY for 9M26), after market hours on 7 October 2026. Its 3Q26
                                            revenue of TWD9,493m (+30.5% QoQ and +87.3% YoY) accounted for a respective 98.4%
                                            and 97.4% of our and Bloomberg consensus estimates for 3Q26 revenue, respectively.

                                            We have a Buy (1) call, with a 12-month TP of TWD10,000, based on a target PER of 73x
                                            applied to our 1-year-forward EPS. For more information on the company, please refer to
                                            our latest flash note, 3Q26 preview: impressive rising ASP trend, on 29 September 2026.

                                            What’s the impact
                                            • 3Q26 revenue: roughly in line. Jentech reported September 2026 revenue of
                                              TWD3,054m (-5.3% MoM and +80.0% YoY; +47.1% YoY for 9M26). Its 3Q26 revenue of
                                              TWD9,493m (+30.5% QoQ and +87.3% YoY) accounted for a respective 98.4% and
                                              97.4% of our (TWD9,650m, +32.7% QoQ and +90.4% YoY) and Bloomberg consensus
                                              estimates for 3Q26 revenue, respectively. Revenue mix in September 2026 is: heat
                                              spreader (79.7%; +94.2% YoY), lead frame (7.8%; +47.9% YoY), electronic components
                                              (4.0%; -12.4% YoY), communications (0.7%; +53.8% YoY) and others (7.7%; +70.8%
                                              YoY); revenue mix in 3Q26 is: heat spreader (79.3%; +107.1% YoY), lead frame (7.2%;
                                              +43.0% YoY), electronic components (3.8%; -4.5% YoY), communication (0.7%; -13.5%
                                              YoY) and others (8.9%; +64.1% YoY).

                                            • Promising rising ASP trend given higher TDP and warpage concerns. Due to rising
                                              thermal design power (TDP) and warpage risk, we expect rising revenue contribution
                                              from removable lids in 2027, with these being implemented in Vera Rubin and Rubin
                                              Ultra from 1Q27E to prevent warpage and increase thermal efficiency. We expect
                                              removable lids to be adopted largely in the next 2-3 years by both GPU and ASIC
                                              clients.


       Important disclosures, including any required research certifications, are provided on the last three pages of this report.
                                              Jentech Precision Industrial (3653 TT)
                                                                             7 October 2026


What we recommend
We have a Buy (1) call, with a 12-month TP of TWD10,000, based on a target PER of 73x
applied to our 1-year-forward EPS. Based on our 2026/27E EPS, the stock is currently
trading at PERs of 98.5x/38.7x, vs. its past-3-year trading range of 16-53x. Key downside
risks: weaker-than-expected global AI server demand; slower-than-expected thermal spec
upgrades.


In the interests of timeliness, this document has not been edited.

                                                                                                                                                 7 October 2026
MEMO


           Asia Vital Components (3017 TT)
           Share price (6 Oct): TWD3,685.00                      12-mth rating: Buy (1)                                          Information Technology: Taiwan


           Record-high 3Q26 revenue beat expectations

       Helen Chien                             Summary: Before the market open on 7 October, AVC reported record-high monthly
       (886) 2 8758 6254                       revenue of TWD21,018m for September 2026 (+7.9% MoM and +44.9% YoY; +71.2% YoY
       helen.chien@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw
                                               for 9M26). Its 3Q26 revenue, also a record-high, accounted for 102.3% and 103.0% of our
       Neil Teng, CFA                          and consensus forecasts, respectively.
       (886) 2 8758 6256
       neil.teng@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw         We have a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP of TWD4,465, based on a target PER of 30x
                                               applied to our one-year-forward EPS estimate. For more information on the company, please
                                               refer to our latest flash note, Revenue momentum heats up, published on 9 September.

                                               What’s the impact
                                               • Record-high 3Q26 revenue slightly beat expectations. Before market open of 7
                                                 October, AVC reported record-high monthly revenue of TWD21,018m for September
                                                 2026 (+7.9% MoM and +44.9% YoY; +71.2% YoY for 9M26). Its 3Q26 revenue of
                                                 TWD59,089m (+20.3% QoQ and +51.8% YoY), also a record-high, accounted for
                                                 102.3% of our forecast (TWD57,771m, +17.6% QoQ and +48.4% YoY) and 103.0% of
                                                 the Bloomberg consensus forecast.

                                               AVC: consolidated monthly sales
                                                   (TWDm)
                                                   25,400                                                                                              200%

                                                   20,400                                                                                              150%

                                                   15,400                                                                                              100%

                                                   10,400                                                                                              50%

                                                    5,400                                                                                              0%

                                                      40 0                                                                                             (50%)


                                                                                            Monthly Sales (LHS)          Growth YoY (RHS)
                                               Source: Company


                                               • 2027 capacity set to expand by 50%+ YoY to support revenue growth. AVC plans to
                                                 expand its cold plate module capacity (mainly in Vietnam) by 50%+ and double its
                                                 capacity for racks and inner manifolds by 2027. AVC said most of the equipment will be
                                                 ready in 2Q27, with production starting in 3Q27. In 2027, we expect higher revenue
                                                 contributions from ASICs and servers, as well as an increase in ASIC liquid-cooling
                                                 penetration rate (ie, 50%+ for one of ASIC client’s project in 2027 vs. 10% in 2026) to
                                                 support gross margin expansion. For 4Q26, we expect revenue momentum to
                                                 strengthen QoQ and continue into 2027.

                                               What we recommend
                                               We have a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP of TWD4,465, based on a target PER of 30x
                                               applied to our one-year-forward EPS estimate. Based on our 2026/27E EPS, the stock is
                                               currently trading at PERs of 34.8x/23.0x, vs. its past-3-year trading range of 5-25x. Key
                                               downside risks: slower-than-expected progress in high gross-margin orders; slower AI
                                               server adoption; an economic downturn weighing on end demand.

                                                                                                                                                 7 October 2026
MEMO


           Fositek Corp (6805 TT)
           Share price (6 Oct): TWD2,415.00                      12-mth rating: Buy (1)                                          Information Technology: Taiwan


           3Q26 revenue largely in line with expectations

       Helen Chien                             Summary: Fositek reported its September 2026 monthly revenue before market hours on
       (886) 2 8758 6254                       7 October 2026. Revenue was TWD1,613m (+5.6% MoM and +32.2% YoY; +47.3% YoY
       helen.chien@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw
                                               for 9M26), a record high. Its 3Q26 revenue accounted for 98.9% and 98.2% of our and
       Neil Teng, CFA                          consensus forecasts, respectively.
       (886) 2 8758 6256
       neil.teng@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw         We have a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP of TWD2,615, based on a target PER of 32x
                                               applied to our one-year-forward EPS estimate. For more information on the company, please
                                               refer to our latest flash note, Investor meeting: positive tone over 2026-27 outlook, published
                                               on 4 August 2026.

                                               What’s the impact
                                               • 3Q26 revenue largely in line with expectations. On 7 October, Fositek reported
                                                 record-high monthly revenue of TWD1,613m for September 2026 (+5.6% MoM and
                                                 +32.2% YoY; +47.3% YoY for 9M26). Its 3Q26 revenue of TWD4,502m (+20.4% QoQ
                                                 and +26.2% YoY) was also a record high and accounted for 98.9% of our forecast
                                                 (TWD4,550m, +21.7% QoQ and +27.6% YoY) and 98.2% of the Bloomberg consensus
                                                 forecast.

                                               • 4Q26 revenue should grow further QoQ. We expect revenue to increase in 4Q26 vs.
                                                 3Q26, with gross margin expanding QoQ as GPU and ASIC projects ramp up in 2H26.
                                                 With rising liquid cooling penetration, broader product applications, and increased QD
                                                 shipments per rack, we expect revenue to grow 40.9% YoY in 2026E and 41.7% YoY in
                                                 2027E.

                                               What we recommend
                                               We have a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP of TWD2,615, based on a target PER of 32x
                                               applied to our one-year-forward EPS estimate. Based on our 2026/27E EPS, the stock is
                                               currently trading at PERs of 40.9x/26.5x, vs. its past-3-year trading range of 9-42x. Key
                                               downside risks: lower-than-expected market share with key clients, slower-than-expected
                                               penetration rate of foldable phones, and geopolitical risks.

                                               In the interests of timeliness, this document has not been edited.

                        Yageo
                        Valuation
                        We set our target price at NT$1,450, based on 35x average 2027E-28E earnings. We value Yageo based on PE as we believe the
                        company’s earnings performance and industry dynamics would be the key focuses of the market. Our target multiple of 35x is
                        at the higher end of the trading range since 2022. During this period the company has gone through the cycles, successfully
                        integrated the acquired business to enhance its product offerings, and started to deliver stable margins and earnings.


                        Risks
                        Key downside risks to our target price and rating include: 1) slower-than-expected demand recovery; 2) intensified peer and
                        pricing competition; 3) execution risks associated with M&A integration and synergies; and 4) FX and interest rate fluctuations.

Company profile

  Established in 1979, Acter Group (Acter) is a leading engineering services provider specialising in

  and chemical delivery systems (20%), consumer industry electromechanical (4%), biomedical (2%) and
  high-tech equipment & materials sales & services (3%).

                                         Acting on the demand for cleanrooms
                                         Why are cleanrooms a bottleneck in the high-tech
                                         industry?
                                         In recent years, cleanrooms have become a critical bottleneck for high-tech industries,
                                         especially semiconductor manufacturing, OSAT, AI hardware, and PCB, mainly because of
                                         its indispensable nature, severe supply-demand imbalance, labour shortages, and high
                                         technical and regulatory barriers.

Cleanrooms are a                         Cleanrooms are an indispensable core infrastructure as they determine product
bottleneck in the high-                  yield and quality stability. Advanced manufacturing nodes in semiconductors,
tech industry, including                 optoelectronics, and biopharmaceuticals require highly particle-free, constant-temperature,
semiconductor foundry,                   and constant-humidity environments to ensure reliable production. As process
memory, and electronic                   technologies continue to advance, such as 2nm node (or even newer nodes) and
assembling                               advanced packaging, existing cleanrooms must be rebuilt, and the complexity of building
                                         new ones thus increases. This keeps overall demand for cleanrooms at high levels.

                                         A severe global supply-demand imbalance with demand for cleanroom construction
                                         outpacing supply. The surge in AI servers, high-performance computing (HPC), and high-
                                         bandwidth memory (HBM) has triggered a global expansion for front-end wafer fabs,

                                         Human resources are an additional limitation to capacity growth. Cleanroom
                                         engineering is highly technical and labour-intensive, relying on specialised on-site
                                         installation and supervision that cannot be replaced by robots. At the same time, the
                                         industry faces severe labour shortages and an aging workforce, and younger generations
                                         are reluctant to join field operations. Cross-border staff deployment is also less cost-
                                         efficient than local hiring.

                                         Cleanrooms involve complex system integration, creating high barriers to entry. A
                                         cleanroom construction includes 4 sequential phases, where each phase usually requires
                                         totally different areas of expertise. Therefore, the competitive landscape in each area
                                         differs. The process begins with civil & structural (C&S) works to establish the physical
                                         plant, followed by mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) works for essential utility
                                         generation, where Acter is one of the leading global experts. After MEP is finished,
                                         chemicals/gas/water are then distributed via main systems through primary piping
                                         network and finally delivered to production equipment through hook-up systems. As

                        global supply chains restructure under N+1 (domestic market + 1) strategies, companies
                        building overseas facilities in places like the US face strict and complicated licensing
                        processes, particularly on fire safety and hazardous chemicals. Without experience dealing
                        with such engineering and safety issues, construction timelines can be severely delayed.

                        As a result, even with advanced equipment and chip designs, a high-tech company cannot
                        begin production without adequate cleanroom space, skilled engineers, and system-
                        integration capabilities. Therefore, cleanroom engineering contractors hold significant
                        bargaining power and capacity allocation leverage in today's tech supply chain.

                        IC foundry
                        In the foundry sector, where the cleanroom supply-demand shortage is the tightest, project
                        activity remains centred on advanced process capacity expansion in Taiwan and Arizona.
                        Simultaneously, domestic advanced node development remains intense, with multi-phase
                        fab builds advancing across Hsinchu, Taichung, and Kaohsiung. Local cleanroom and MEP
                        integration demand is further boosted by advanced packaging facilities in Taiwan (such as
                        Chiayi and Tainan) and upcoming projects in the US are set to contribute revenue for the
                        cleanroom providers in the following years.

                        Memory
                        The memory segment is exhibiting robust momentum as well, mainly catalysed by HBM
                        capacity additions. Projects such as the plant in Japan, transitioned to contribution for the
                        cleanroom EPCM providers starting from 2026. In Taiwan, turnkey engineering contracts in
                        Miaoli are also actively underway. This trend is reinforced by stronger-than-expected
                        expansion activity from memory producers in China.

                        OSAT, PCB and ODM/OEM
                        For OSAT companies, demand is also surging due to the spill-over effect of advanced
                        packaging protocols and N+1 supply chain restructuring. The OSAT names are expanding
                        their footprint both in Southern Taiwan and in overseas locations including in the US and
                        Southeast Asia. Major engineering contracts signed between OSAT clients and Acter show
                        stable long-term workload for strong cleanroom demand over our forecast horizon.
                        Similarly, overseas expansion for PCB manufacturing is peaking in Southeast Asia,
                        especially in Thailand. We expect Chinese PCB players to also increase their capacity, just
                        like memory companies in the past year. Except for front-end and back-end chip
                        manufacturing, ODM/OEM and data centre infrastructure is also a key growth engine for
                        the EPCM industry. Major Taiwanese ODMs are building production facilities in Texas and
                        Mexico to meet local manufacturing needs. Cleanroom contractors, such as Acter,
                        providing MEP and system integration in Texas are directly benefiting from these projects.
                        The shift toward liquid cooling systems has also increased engineering complexity,
                        favouring few cleanroom companies with the expertise to deliver complex integration for
                        CSPs in both North America and Southeast Asia.
